units.zh: 《書》曰：「唐虞稽古，建官惟百。」
units.en: The Book of Documents says: "When Tang and Yu looked back to antiquity, they created no more than a hundred offices."
units.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Tang and Yu examined antiquity; they established offices numbering only one hundred."

units.zh: 所以獎導民萌，裁成庶政。
units.en: That was how they encouraged the people and gave shape to the affairs of state.
units.literal: By this means they encouraged and guided the common people, and brought order to every branch of government.

units.zh: 《易》曰：「天垂象，聖人則之。」
units.en: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven displays signs; the sage patterns himself on them."
units.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven hangs forth images; the sage takes them as his model."

units.zh: 執法在南宮之右，上相處端門之外，而鳥龍居位，雲火垂名，前史詳之，其以尚矣。
units.en: Justice lay to the right of the Southern Palace; the chief minister waited beyond the Duan Gate; bird and dragon offices held rank with cloud and fire as their emblems—prior histories lay it out clearly, and the grandeur speaks for itself.
units.literal: Law sat to the right of the Southern Palace; the chief minister took station beyond the Duan Gate; the Bird and Dragon offices held their posts, cloud and fire lending their names—earlier histories spell this out in detail, and the dignity of it is plain.

units.zh: 黃帝置三公之秩，以親黎元，少昊配九扈之名，以為農正，命重黎於天地，詔融冥於水火，則可得而言焉。
units.en: The Yellow Emperor created the Three Dukes to draw near to the people; Shaohao aligned the Nine Hu titles with agricultural oversight; Chong and Li received Heaven and Earth; Zhu Rong and Ming received fire and water—and such patterns can be put into words.
units.literal: The Yellow Emperor instituted the ranks of the Three Dukes to stay close to the black-haired masses; Shaohao paired the Nine Hu bird-names with the office of director of agriculture; Chong and Li were charged with Heaven and Earth; Zhu Rong and Ming were charged with fire and water—these arrangements can indeed be described.

units.zh: 伊尹曰：「三公調陰陽，九卿通寒暑，大夫知人事，列士去其私。」
units.en: Yi Yin said: "The Three Dukes harmonize yin and yang; the Nine Ministers track the seasons; grand officers attend to human affairs; ranked officers put private interest aside."
units.literal: Yi Yin said: "The Three Dukes harmonize yin and yang; the Nine Ministers watch cold and heat; grand officers understand human affairs; ranked officers rid themselves of selfishness."

units.zh: 而成湯居亳，初置二相，以伊尹、仲虺為之，凡厥樞會，仰承君命。
units.en: When Tang of Shang made Bo his seat, he first set up two chancellors—Yi Yin and Zhong Hui—and on every pivot they carried out the sovereign's will.
units.literal: When Cheng Tang ruled from Bo, he first created two chancellors and appointed Yi Yin and Zhong Hui to them; on every critical matter they looked upward to receive the ruler's commands.

units.zh: 總及周武下車，成康垂則，六卿分職，二公弘化，咸樹司存，各題標準，苟非其道，人弗虛榮。
units.en: Under King Wu and the models left by Cheng and Kang, the Six Ministers split the labor, the Two Dukes carried royal influence abroad, every bureau had its charter, and no one claimed idle honors without the right conduct.
units.literal: Altogether, when King Wu of Zhou stepped down from his chariot to rule, Cheng and Kang handed down norms; the Six Ministers divided duties; the Two Dukes spread transformation; each office kept its place and measure; if it were not the proper Way, people did not vainly seek glory.

units.zh: 貽厥孫謀，其固本也如此。
units.en: They anchored the dynasty by planning for generations yet unborn.
units.literal: They left plans for their descendants; thus they secured the foundation.

units.zh: 及秦變周官，漢遵嬴舊，或隨時適用，或因務遷革，霸王之典，義在於斯，既獲厥安，所謂得其時制者也。
units.en: Qin refashioned Zhou's bureaucracy; Han largely kept Qin's frame while tweaking it for the moment—the logic of strong rule was there—and stability meant institutions matched their age.
units.literal: When Qin altered the Zhou offices and Han followed the Ying-clan precedent, sometimes adapting to the times, sometimes shifting with practical needs—the norms of hegemons and kings lay herein; once stability was gained, this is what is called obtaining timely institutions.

units.zh: 四征興於漢代，四安起于魏初，四鎮通於柔遠，四平止於喪亂，其渡遼、淩江，輕車、強弩，式揚遐外，用表攻伐，興而復毀，厥號彌繁。
units.en: Han invented the Four Expeditions; Wei at its outset the Four Pacifications; Four Garrisons stretched toward distant peoples; Four Peace posts vanished when chaos returned. Epithets like Crossing-the-Liao, River-Fording, light chariot, and strong crossbow brandished force beyond the borders for campaigns—created, scrapped, then multiplied until the catalogue grew tangled.
units.literal: The Four Expeditions arose in Han; the Four Pacifications began at the start of Wei; the Four Garrisons reached outward to soothe the distant; the Four Peace offices ended with turmoil and disorder; as for Crossing-the-Liao, River-Fording, light chariot, and strong crossbow—they displayed might afar and signaled campaigns—raised up and then abolished, their titles grew ever more numerous.

units.zh: 及當塗得志，克平諸夏，初有軍師祭酒，參掌戎律。
units.en: Once the Cao regime triumphed and pacified the heartland, it introduced the army adviser libationer to share oversight of military law.
units.literal: When the house at Dangtu achieved its ambition and subdued the Central Plain, there first appeared the army adviser libationer, who jointly handled military regulations.

units.zh: 建安十三年，罷漢台司，更置丞相，而以曹公居之，用兼端揆。
units.en: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an (208), the Han ministerial posts were abolished, the chancellorship was reinstated, and Lord Cao held it, thereby combining the highest civil authority.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an, the Han terrace ministers were abolished; the chancellor was reinstated, and Lord Cao held it, thereby combining the highest civil authority.

units.zh: 孫吳、劉蜀，多依漢制，雖復臨時命氏，而無忝舊章。
units.en: Wu and Shu largely kept Han models; occasional improvised titles notwithstanding, they stayed within the classical mold.
units.literal: Eastern Wu and Liu Bei's Shu largely followed Han institutions; though they sometimes improvised titles on the spot, they did not shame the old statutes.

units.zh: 世祖武皇帝即位之初，以安平王孚為太宰，鄭沖為太傅，王祥為太保，司馬望為太尉，何曾為司徒，荀顗為司空，石苞為大司馬，陳騫為大將軍，世所謂八公同辰，攀雲附翼者也。
units.en: At his accession, Emperor Wu named Sima Fu Grand Preceptor, Zheng Chong Grand Tutor, Wang Xiang Grand Guardian, Sima Wang Minister of War, He Zeng Minister of Education, Xun Yi Minister of Works, Shi Bao Grand Marshal, and Chen Qian Grand General—the storied eight dukes of a single hour, men who rose by riding imperial favor.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu the Shizu first ascended the throne, he appointed Prince Fu of Anping as Grand Preceptor, Zheng Chong as Grand Tutor, Wang Xiang as Grand Guardian, Sima Wang as Minister of War, He Zeng as Minister of Education, Xun Yi as Minister of Works, Shi Bao as Grand Marshal, and Chen Qian as Grand General—what the age called the eight dukes sharing one hour, climbing clouds and attaching wings.

units.zh: 若乃成乎棟宇，非一枝之勢；
units.en: Raising the whole hall takes more than one timber;
units.literal: As for completing roof-beams and rafters—it is not the strength of a single branch;

units.zh: 處乎經綸，稱萬夫之敵。
units.en: true stewardship of the realm earns the title match for ten thousand.
units.literal: to dwell in ordering the realm is to be called a match for ten thousand men.

units.zh: 或牽羊以葉於夢，或垂釣以申其道，或空桑以獻其術，或操版以啟其心。
units.en: Some arrived through dreams of sheep and grain; some through fishing metaphors; some from humble soil with a craft to sell; some by presenting the royal tablet and winning trust.
units.literal: Some led sheep and answered a leaf in a dream; some angled with a hook to proclaim their Way; some offered their arts from an empty mulberry; some grasped the tablet to open the ruler's mind.

units.zh: 臥龍飛鴻，方金擬璧，秦奚、鄭產，楚材晉用，斯亦曩時之良具，其又昭彰者焉。
units.en: Hidden dragons and soaring swans, talents weighed like gold against jade—Qin Xi, Zheng Chan, and Chu talent employed by Jin: these too were fine instruments of former times, and no less manifest.
units.literal: The sleeping dragon, the soaring wild goose—square metal compared to round jade; the shepherd of Qin, the prodigy of Zheng; Chu talent employed by Jin—these too were fine instruments of former times, and no less manifest.

units.zh: 宣王既誅曹爽，政由己出，網羅英俊，以備天官。
units.en: After Sima Yi eliminated Cao Shuang, he ruled in his own name and stocked every court post with talent.
units.literal: Once Prince Xuan had executed Cao Shuang, government proceeded from himself alone; he gathered capable men to fill the celestial offices.

units.zh: 及蘭卿受羈，貴公顯戮，雖復策名魏氏，而乃心皇晉。
units.en: When fine officers were seized and great nobles died in public execution, names might still stand with Wei but hearts had already turned to Jin.
units.literal: When worthy ministers were placed under restraint and eminent dukes suffered public execution—though they still bore registration under the Wei, their hearts were with the august Jin.

units.zh: 及文王纂業，初啟晉台，始置二衛，有前驅養由之弩；
units.en: When Sima Zhao extended the family work and founded the Jin apparatus, he created the Two Guards with vanguard crossbows worthy of Yang Youji.
units.literal: When King Wen continued the enterprise and first opened the Jin terrace, he began setting up the Two Guards, including front-vanguard crossbows like Yang Youji's.

units.zh: 及設三部，有熊渠佽飛之眾。
units.en: When the Three Corps were established, there were masses like those of Xiong Qu and Ci Fei.
units.literal: When the Three Departments were established, there were masses like the royal swimmers of Xiong Qu.

units.zh: 是以武帝龍飛，乘茲奮翼，猶武王以周之十亂而理殷民者也。
units.en: Thus Emperor Wu's rise—vaulting on these preparations—matched King Wu deploying his ten able assistants to rule the former Shang subjects.
units.literal: Therefore when Emperor Wu ascended like a dragon, riding this to beat his wings, it was like King Wu of Zhou using the Zhou's ten ministers to govern the Yin people.

units.zh: 是以泰始盡于太康，喬柯茂葉，來居斯位；
units.en: From the Taishi era through Taikang, imposing figures filled those ranks;
units.literal: Thus from Taishi through Taikang, tall trees with lush foliage came to occupy these posts;

units.zh: 自太興訖於建元，南金北銑，用處茲秩。
units.en: from Daxing to Jianyuan, the finest metal south and north filled those offices.
units.literal: from Daxing down to Jianyuan, southern gold and northern ore were employed in these ranks.

units.zh: 雖未擬乎夔拊龍言，天工人代，亦庶幾乎任官惟賢，蒞事惟能者也。
units.en: They fell short of the sage-kings' marriage of Heaven's work to human agency, yet they neared the ideal: office by virtue, tasks by competence.
units.literal: Though they did not equal Kui's drumming and Long's pronouncements—Heaven's work and man's substitute—they approximated appoint officials only for worth, approach affairs only by ability.

units.zh: 丞相、相國，並秦官也。
units.en: The titles chancellor and minister of state both originated in Qin.
units.literal: Chancellor and minister of state were both Qin offices.

units.zh: 晉受魏禪，並不置，自惠帝之後，省置無恆。
units.en: Jin left both vacant at the founding; after Emperor Hui the posts flickered in and out without a fixed rule.
units.literal: When Jin received Wei's abdication, neither was established; from Emperor Hui onward, abolition and establishment were not constant.

units.zh: 為之者，趙王倫、梁王肜、成都王穎、南陽王保、王敦、王導之徒，皆非復尋常人臣之職。
units.en: When princes such as Sima Lun, Sima Rong, Sima Ying, Sima Bao, Wang Dun, and Wang Dao took these titles, they wielded power far beyond an ordinary subject's charge.
units.literal: Those who held them—Zhao Wang Lun, Liang Wang Rong, Chengdu Wang Ying, Nanyang Wang Bao, Wang Dun, Wang Dao, and the like—were no longer the duties of ordinary ministers.

units.zh: 太宰、太傅、太保，周之三公官也。
units.en: Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Guardian were Zhou's classical Three Dukes.
units.literal: Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Guardian were the Three Dukes of Zhou.

units.zh: 魏初唯置太傅，以鐘繇為之，末年又置太保，以鄭沖為之。
units.en: Early Wei appointed only a Grand Tutor—Zhong Yao—and near the dynasty's end added a Grand Guardian, Zheng Chong.
units.literal: At the start of Wei only Grand Tutor was set up, with Zhong Yao holding it; toward the end Grand Guardian was added, with Zheng Chong holding it.

units.zh: 晉初以景帝諱故，又采《周官》官名，置太宰以代太師之任，秩增三司，與太傅太保皆為上公，論道經邦，燮理陰陽，無其人則闕。
units.en: Early Jin avoided the taboo on Sima Shi's name and borrowed Zhou ritual titles: Grand Preceptor replaced Grand Instructor, ranked above the Three Departments alongside Grand Tutor and Grand Guardian as upper dukes who counseled on the Way and the realm and balanced yin and yang—and remained empty when no one qualified.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jin, because of the taboo on Emperor Jing's name, and adopting titles from the Offices of Zhou, Grand Preceptor was established in place of Grand Instructor; the rank was raised above the Three Departments; together with Grand Tutor and Grand Guardian they formed the upper dukes, discussing the Way and ordering the state, harmonizing yin and yang; if there was no suitable person the post stayed vacant.

units.zh: 以安平獻王孚居之。
units.en: The office went to Sima Fu, Prince Xian of Anping.
units.literal: Prince Xian of Anping, Fu, occupied it.

units.zh: 自渡江以後，其名不替，而居之者甚寡。
units.en: South of the Yangzi the title survived, yet almost nobody actually held it.
units.literal: After crossing the river the name was not dropped, but those who held it were very few.

units.zh: 太尉、司徒、司空，並古官也。
units.en: The ministers of war, education, and works were ancient posts.
units.literal: Minister of War, Minister of Education, and Minister of Works are all ancient offices.

units.zh: 自漢曆魏，置以為三公。
units.en: Han and Wei treated them as the Three Dukes.
units.literal: From Han through Wei they were established as the Three Dukes.

units.zh: 及晉受命，迄江左，其官相承不替。
units.en: From Jin's founding through the southern court the succession never broke.
units.literal: When Jin received the mandate down to the Jiang left, these offices continued in unbroken succession.

units.zh: 大司馬，古官也。
units.en: The Grand Marshal was an ancient title.
units.literal: Grand Marshal is an ancient office.

units.zh: 漢制以冠大將軍、驃騎、車騎之上，以代太尉之職，故恆與太尉迭置，不並列。
units.en: Han ranked it above the chief generals as stand-in for Minister of War, so it rotated with that office rather than sitting beside it.
units.literal: Han regulations placed it above Grand General, Cavalry-in-Chief, and Chariots-in-Chief, substituting for the Minister of War; therefore it alternated with the Minister of War and was not held concurrently.

units.zh: 及魏有太尉，而大司馬、大將軍各自為官，位在三司上。
units.en: Under Wei the Minister of War returned as its own post while Grand Marshal and Grand General sat above the Three Departments.
units.literal: When Wei had a Minister of War, Grand Marshal and Grand General each became separate offices, ranking above the Three Departments.

units.zh: 晉受魏禪，因其制，以安平王孚為太宰，鄭沖為太傅。
units.en: Jin kept Wei's scheme: Sima Fu as Grand Preceptor, Zheng Chong as Grand Tutor.
units.literal: When Jin received Wei's abdication, following that system, Prince Fu of Anping became Grand Preceptor and Zheng Chong Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 王祥為太保，義陽王望為太尉，何曾為司徒，荀顗為司空，石苞為大司馬，陳騫為大將軍，凡八公同時並置，唯無丞相焉。
units.en: Wang Xiang became Grand Guardian, Sima Wang Minister of War, He Zeng Minister of Education, Xun Yi Minister of Works, Shi Bao Grand Marshal, Chen Qian Grand General—all eight peers at once, the chancellor alone omitted.
units.literal: Wang Xiang as Grand Guardian, Prince Wang of Yiyang as Minister of War, He Zeng as Minister of Education, Xun Yi as Minister of Works, Shi Bao as Grand Marshal, Chen Qian as Grand General—in all eight dukes were established at once; only the chancellor was missing.

units.zh: 自義陽王望為大司馬之後，定令如舊，在三司上。
units.en: After Sima Wang took Grand Marshal, statute fixed it as before—above the Three Departments.
units.literal: After Prince Wang of Yiyang became Grand Marshal, the fixed regulations were as before: it ranked above the Three Departments.

units.zh: 大將軍，古官也。
units.en: Grand General was an ancient office.
units.literal: Grand General was an ancient office.

units.zh: 漢武帝置，冠以大司馬名，為崇重之職。
units.en: Han Wudi created it, lending it the Grand Marshal name as a post of exceptional weight.
units.literal: Emperor Wu of Han established it, crowning it with the Grand Marshal name as a weighty and honored post.

units.zh: 及漢東京，大將軍不常置，為之者皆擅朝權。
units.en: In Eastern Han it was irregular, and every holder seized court power.
units.literal: By Eastern Han at Luoyang the Grand General was not regularly established; those who held it all monopolized court power.

units.zh: 至景帝為大將軍，亦受非常之任。
units.en: When Sima Jing became Grand General he too received an extraordinary commission.
units.literal: When Jingdi became Grand General he also received an extraordinary commission.

units.zh: 後以叔父孚為太尉，奏改大將軍在太尉下。
units.en: Later Uncle Sima Fu as Minister of War moved the Grand General below that office.
units.literal: Later when Uncle Fu became Minister of War, he memorialized to place the Grand General below the Minister of War.

units.zh: 及晉受命，猶依其制，位次三司下，後復舊，在三司上。
units.en: Jin first kept it below the Three Departments, then restored it above them.
units.literal: When Jin received the mandate they still followed this system, ranking below the Three Departments; later they restored the old order, above the Three Departments.

units.zh: 太康元年，琅邪王伷遷大將軍，復制在三司下，伷薨後如舊。
units.en: In 280 Prince You of Langye as Grand General again ranked below the Three Departments until his death restored the old order.
units.literal: In the first year of Taikang Prince You of Langye was transferred to Grand General and the regulation was again below the Three Departments; after You died it returned as before.

units.zh: 開府儀同三司，漢官也。
units.en: Opening a headquarters with ritual parity with the Three Excellencies was a Han office.
units.literal: Establishing a headquarters with ceremonies equal to the Three Departments is a Han office.

units.zh: 殤帝延平元年，鄭騭為車騎將軍，儀同三司；
units.en: In 106 CE Emperor Shang named Zheng Zhi chariot-and-cavalry general with Three-Department ceremonial rank;
units.literal: In the first year of Yanping of Emperor Shang, Zheng Zhi was chariots-and-cavalry general with ritual parity with the Three Departments;

units.zh: 儀同之名，始自此也。
units.en: that is when ritual parity first appears.
units.literal: the name ritual parity begins from this.

units.zh: 及魏黃權以車騎將軍開府儀同三司；
units.en: Wei later gave Huang Quan chariot command, full headquarters, and Three-Department parity;
units.literal: When Wei made Huang Quan chariot-and-cavalry general who established headquarters with ritual parity with the Three Departments;

units.zh: 開府之名，起於此也。
units.en: the establish headquarters formula dates from then.
units.literal: the name establish headquarters arises from this.

units.zh: 驃騎、車騎、衛將軍、伏波、撫軍、都護、鎮軍、中軍、四征、四鎮、龍驤、典軍、上軍、輔國等大將軍，左右光祿、光祿三大夫，開府者皆為位從公。
units.en: Grand generals of Agile Cavalry, Chariots and Cavalry, Guards, Wave-Quelling, Army-Pacifying, Chief Protector, Garrison Army, Central Army, the Four Expeditions, the Four Garrisons, Dragon-Soaring, Army Directorate, Upper Army, State-Supporting, and similar commands, along with the left and right Grand Masters of Splendid Happiness and the three Grand Masters of Splendid Happiness, ranked next to the dukes when they opened headquarters.
units.literal: Grand Generals of Agile Cavalry, Chariots and Cavalry, Guards, Wave-Quelling, Army-Pacifying, Chief Protector, Garrison Army, Central Army, the Four Expeditions, the Four Garrisons, Dragon-Soaring, Army Directorate, Upper Army, State-Supporting, and the like, together with the left and right Grand Masters of Splendid Happiness and the three Grand Masters of Splendid Happiness—those who established headquarters all ranked next to the dukes.

units.zh: 太宰、太傅、太保、司徒、司空、左右光祿大夫、光祿大夫，開府位從公者為文官公，冠進賢三梁，黑介幘。
units.en: Civil dukes ranked next to the full dukes included the Grand Steward, Grand Tutor, Grand Guardian, Minister over the Masses, Minister of Works, the left and right Grand Masters of Splendid Happiness, and the Grand Masters of Splendid Happiness; they wore the three-ridged Jinxian cap and a black kerchief.
units.literal: Grand Steward, Grand Tutor, Grand Guardian, Minister over the Masses, Minister of Works, Left and Right Grand Masters of Splendid Happiness, and Grand Masters of Splendid Happiness—those who opened headquarters and ranked next to dukes were civil dukes; they wore the three-rib Jinxian cap with a black scarf.

units.zh: 大司馬、大將軍、太尉、驃騎、車騎、衛將軍、諸大將軍，開府位從公者為武官公，皆著武冠，平上黑幘。
units.en: Military junior dukes—the top martial posts with full headquarters—wore the warrior's cap and flat black scarf.
units.literal: Grand Marshal, Grand General, Minister of War, cavalry-in-Chief, chariots-in-Chief, guards general, various grand generals—those who opened headquarters as secondary to dukes were military dukes; all wore military caps with flat-top black scarves.

units.zh: 文武官公，皆假金章紫綬，著五時服。
units.en: Both kinds bore gold seals on purple cords and seasonal court dress.
units.literal: Civil and military dukes all wore gold seals with purple ribbons and the five-seasons robes.

units.zh: 其相國、丞相，皆袞冕，綠盭綬，所以殊于常公也。
units.en: Chancellors and ministers of state alone wore full ritual robes and green ribbons—marking them above ordinary peers.
units.literal: Ministers of state and chancellors wore coronation robes and caps with green twisted ribbons—whereby they differed from ordinary dukes.

units.zh: 諸公及開府位從公者，品秩第一，食奉日五斛。
units.en: Dukes and junior peers ranked first grade with five hu of grain daily.
units.literal: For dukes and secondary dukes with headquarters, grade rank was first; daily grain allowance was five hu.

units.zh: 太康二年，又給絹，春百匹，秋絹二百匹，綿二百斤。
units.en: From 281 they also received silk—one hundred bolts each spring, two hundred each autumn, and two hundred jin of cotton.
units.literal: In the second year of Taikang silk was also granted—one hundred bolts in spring, two hundred bolts of silk in autumn, and two hundred jin of cotton.

units.zh: 元康元年，給菜田十頃，田騶十人，立夏後不及田者，食奉一年。
units.en: In 291 they received ten qing of kitchen gardens and ten field grooms; anyone unable to take land after Start of Summer drew a year's stipend instead.
units.literal: In the first year of Yuankang they were granted ten qing of vegetable fields and ten field grooms; those who could not take up fields after the Start of Summer received one year's grain allowance.

units.zh: 置長史一人，秩一千石；
units.en: They had one chief clerk at one thousand shi;
units.literal: One chief clerk was established at rank one thousand shi;

units.zh: 西東閣祭酒、西東曹掾、戶倉賊曹令史屬各一人；
units.en: one pavilion libationer east and west, one bureau staff east and west, and one clerk each for household, granary, and thieves offices;
units.literal: one libationer each for the western and eastern pavilions, one staff member each for the western and eastern bureaus, and one clerk and aide each for household, granary, and thieves offices;

units.zh: 禦屬閣下令史、西東曹倉戶賊曹令史、門令史、記室省事令史、閣下記室書令史、西東曹學事各一人。
units.en: plus imperial-staff clerks, granary and household clerks, gate and secretary clerks, and one academic officer per eastern and western bureau.
units.literal: one clerk under the imperial staff pavilion, clerks for the western and eastern bureaus of granary, household, and thieves offices, gate clerks, secretary and efficiency clerks, pavilion secretaries, and one academic officer each for the western and eastern bureaus.

units.zh: 給武賁二十人，持班劍。
units.en: Twenty martial guards with ceremonial swords were assigned.
units.literal: Twenty martial guards were supplied, bearing ceremonial swords.

units.zh: 給朝車駕駟、安車黑耳駕三各一乘，祭酒掾屬白蓋小車七乘，軺車施耳後戶、皁輪犢車各一乘。
units.en: Their transport included a four-horse court carriage, secure and black-eared carriages, seven white-canopied staff carts, and light and black-wheeled calf carriages.
units.literal: They received one court carriage with four-horse team, one each of secure carriage and black-eared carriage with three horses, seven white-canopied small carriages for libationers and staff, and one each of light carriage with rear door and black-wheeled calf carriage.

units.zh: 自祭酒已下，令史已上，皆皁零辟朝服。
units.en: From libationers through clerks they wore black-bordered court robes.
units.literal: From libationers downward and clerks upward—all wore black border court robes.

units.zh: 太尉雖不加兵者，吏屬皆絳服。
units.en: Even unarmed Ministers of War dressed their staffs in crimson.
units.literal: Even when the Minister of War held no added military authority, clerks and staff all wore crimson robes.

units.zh: 司徒加置左右長史各一人，秩千石；
units.en: The Minister of Education added left and right chief clerks at one thousand shi;
units.literal: The Minister of Education added one left and one right chief clerk each at one thousand shi;

units.zh: 主簿、左西曹掾屬各一人，西曹稱右西曹，其左西曹令史已下人數如舊令。
units.en: one chief clerk and one western-bureau aide—the western bureau was styled right western bureau, with left-bureau clerks as in the old code.
units.literal: one chief clerk and one western-bureau staff member each; the western bureau was called the right western bureau, and the number of clerks under the left western bureau followed the old regulations.

units.zh: 司空加置導橋掾一人。
units.en: The Minister of Works added one bridge-guide aide.
units.literal: The Minister of Works added one bridge-guide staff member.

units.zh: 諸公及開府位從公加兵者，增置司馬一人，秩千石；
units.en: Junior dukes with troops added one adjutant at one thousand shi salary;
units.literal: For dukes and secondary dukes with headquarters who held military authority, one adjutant was added at rank one thousand shi;

units.zh: 從事中郎二人，秩比千石；
units.en: two senior staff officers at near-thousand-shi pay;
units.literal: two attendant gentlemen-inside at salary comparable to one thousand shi;

units.zh: 主簿、記室督各一人；
units.en: one chief clerk and one secretary supervisor;
units.literal: one chief clerk and one secretary supervisor each;

units.zh: 舍人四人；
units.en: four attendants;
units.literal: four gentlemen-attendants;

units.zh: 兵鎧、士曹，營軍、刺奸、帳下都督，外都督，令史各一人。
units.en: single posts for armor, personnel, camp affairs, discipline, household guard, external command, and records.
units.literal: one each for armor office, gentlemen office, camp army, inspector of malfeasance, household-area commander, external commander, and clerks.

units.zh: 主簿已下，令史已上，皆絳服。
units.en: Staff from chief clerk through clerks wore crimson.
units.literal: From chief clerk downward and clerk upward—all wore crimson robes.

units.zh: 司馬給吏卒如長史，從事中郎給侍二人，主簿、記室督各給侍一人。
units.en: Adjutants received runners like chief clerks; attendant gentlemen got two pages; chief clerk and secretary one each.
units.literal: The adjutant was supplied clerks and runners like the chief clerk; each attendant gentleman-inside received two attendants; chief clerk and secretary supervisor each received one attendant.

units.zh: 其餘臨時增崇者，則褒加各因其時為節文，不為定制。
units.en: Ad hoc honors followed occasion and were never codified.
units.literal: Other temporary elevations followed seasonal commendations as circumstances demanded; they were not fixed regulations.

units.zh: 諸公及開府位從公為持節都督，增參車為六人，長史、司馬、從事中郎、主簿、記室督、祭酒、掾屬、舍人如常加兵公制。
units.en: When dukes and open-headquarters officials ranked next to dukes served as credential-bearing area commanders, they had six advisory carriages; their chief administrators, marshals, attendant gentlemen, registrars, records supervisors, libationers, staff, and attendants followed the regular military-duke regulations.
units.literal: When dukes and those who opened headquarters and ranked next to dukes became credential-bearing area commanders, advisory carriages were increased to six; the chief administrator, marshal, attendant gentleman, registrar, records supervisor, libationer, staff, and attendants followed the regular regulations for dukes with military commands.

units.zh: 特進，漢官也。
units.en: Extraordinary Advancement was Han in origin.
units.literal: Extraordinary Advancement was a Han office.

units.zh: 二漢及魏晉以加官從本官車服。
units.en: Under Han, Wei, and Jin it was a supernumerary rank following one's primary office for carriages and dress.
units.literal: In the Two Han and Wei-Jin it was a supernumerary office following the carriages and robes of the original office.

units.zh: 無吏卒。
units.en: It carried no clerks or runners.
units.literal: It had no clerks or runners.

units.zh: 太僕羊琇遜位，拜特進，加散騎常侍，無餘官，故給吏卒車服。
units.en: When Yang Xiu of the Imperial Stud retired to Extraordinary Advancement with no other post, he alone received full staff, carriages, and robes.
units.literal: Minister of the Imperial Stud Yang Xiu yielded his post, was appointed Extraordinary Advancement with added Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and had no other office—therefore clerks, runners, carriages, and robes were granted.

units.zh: 其餘加特進者，唯食其祿賜，位其班位而已，不別給特進吏卒車服，後定令。
units.en: Later appointees took only stipend and precedence, not separate extraordinary-advancement perquisites—eventually codified.
units.literal: Others granted Extraordinary Advancement received only stipends and precedence seating—no separate Extraordinary Advancement clerks, runners, carriages, or robes; this was later fixed by statute.

units.zh: 特進品秩第二，位次諸公，在開府驃騎上，冠進賢兩梁，黑介幘，五時朝服，佩水蒼玉，無章綬，食奉日四斛。
units.en: Extraordinary Advancement ranked second after dukes and above cavalry-in-chief peers, with two-ridged cap, black kerchief, seasonal court dress, dark jade, no ribbon seal, and four hu daily.
units.literal: Extraordinary Advancement was grade rank second, ranking after dukes and above headquarters Cavalry-in-Chief; he wore the two-beam advanced-worth cap, black inner kerchief, five-seasons court dress, dark aquamarine jade at the belt, no ribbon seal, and a daily grain allowance of four hu.

units.zh: 太康二年，始賜春服絹五十匹，秋絹百五十匹，綿一百五十斤。
units.en: From 281 they received fifty bolts of spring silk, one hundred fifty of autumn silk, and one hundred fifty jin of cotton.
units.literal: In the second year of Taikang spring robes of fifty bolts of silk were first granted, one hundred fifty bolts in autumn, and one hundred fifty jin of cotton.

units.zh: 元康元年，給菜田八頃，田騶八人，立夏後不及田者，食奉一年。
units.en: In 291 they received eight qing of kitchen gardens and eight field grooms, or a year's stipend if land came too late after Start of Summer.
units.literal: In the first year of Yuankang eight qing of vegetable fields and eight field grooms were granted; those who could not take up fields after Start of Summer received one year's grain allowance.

units.zh: 置主簿、功曹史、門亭長、門下書佐各一人，給安車黑耳駕御一人，軺車施耳後戶一乘。
units.en: Staff included chief clerk, merit clerk, gate chief, and household scribe, plus a secure black-eared carriage and a light carriage with a rear door.
units.literal: One chief clerk, merit clerk, gate pavilion chief, and household scribe were established; one secure carriage with black-eared team and driver, and one light carriage with rear door were granted.

units.zh: 左右光祿大夫，假金章紫綬。
units.en: Senior Splendid Luminaries wore gold-and-purple insignia.
units.literal: Left and right splendid luminaries grandees wore gold seals with purple ribbons.

units.zh: 光祿大夫加金章紫綬者，品秩第二，祿賜、班位、冠幘、車服、佩玉，置吏卒羽林及卒，諸所賜給皆與特進同。
units.en: Gold-purple Splendid Luminaries ranked second grade with stipends, precedence, dress, carriages, jade, and guards matching special advancement.
units.literal: Splendid luminaries grandees granted gold seal and purple ribbon were grade two; stipends, seating, caps, carriages, robes, jade pendants, clerks, runners, feathered-forest guards—all grants matched extraordinary-advance status.

units.zh: 其以為加官者，唯假章綬、祿賜班位而已，不別給車服吏卒也。
units.en: Supernumerary appointees received only insignia and pay—not full perquisites.
units.literal: Those who held it as supernumerary office received only seals, ribbons, stipends, and seating—not separate carriages, robes, clerks, or runners.

units.zh: 又卒贈此位，本已有卿官者，不復重給吏卒，其餘皆給。
units.en: Posthumous awards skipped duplicate runners for men already at minister rank; others received full suites.
units.literal: Moreover, posthumous grants to this rank: if the deceased already held minister rank, runners were not granted again; otherwise all were supplied.

units.zh: 光祿大夫假銀章青綬者，品秩第三，位在金紫將軍下，諸卿上。
units.en: Silver-blue Splendid Luminaries ranked third—below gold-purple generals but above ordinary ministers.
units.literal: Splendid luminaries grandees with silver seal and blue ribbon were grade three, below gold-purple generals and above the various ministers.

units.zh: 漢時所置無定員，多以為拜假賵贈之使，及監護喪事。
units.en: Han used them flexibly—often as ceremonial envoys or funeral supervisors.
units.literal: In Han there was no fixed quota; they were often used as envoys for investitures, gifts, and funeral oversight.

units.zh: 魏氏已來，轉復優重，不復以為使命之官。
units.en: After Wei they became honorific rather than errand posts.
units.literal: Since Wei they grew steadily weightier and ceased to be mere mission offices.

units.zh: 其諸公告老者，皆家拜此位；
units.en: Retiring dukes typically received this title by domestic edict;
units.literal: When various dukes retired, they were all appointed to this rank at home;

units.zh: 及在朝顯職，復用加之，及晉受命，仍舊不改，復以為優崇之制。
units.en: Active ministers might earn it too; Jin kept the practice as a mark of esteem.
units.literal: and for prominent posts at court it was again conferred; when Jin received the mandate it continued unchanged, again treating it as a system of honor.

units.zh: 而諸公遜位，不復加之，或更拜上公，或以本封食公祿。
units.en: Stepping-down dukes did not receive it again—some became upper dukes, others lived on fief income.
units.literal: But when dukes yielded office they were not given it again; some were promoted to upper duke, some drew duke stipends from their original fiefs.

units.zh: 其諸卿尹中朝大官年老致仕者，及內外之職加此者，前後甚眾。
units.en: Many retired ministers and officials inside and outside received it.
units.literal: Among ministers and capital officials who retired for age, and inner and outer posts given this rank, there were very many over time.

units.zh: 由是或因得開府，或進加金章紫綬，又復以為禮贈之位。
units.en: Some parlayed it into a headquarters appointment or gold-purple rank; it doubled as a ceremonial posthumous grade.
units.literal: Hence some thereby gained headquarters, some advanced to gold seal and purple ribbon; it also served as a courtesy gift rank.

units.zh: 泰始中，唯太子詹事楊珧加給事中光祿大夫。
units.en: During Taishi only Yang Yao combined household supervisor with attendant-within and Splendid Luminaries.
units.literal: In Taishi only Yang Yao, supervisor of the heir apparent's household, was additionally appointed attendant-within and splendid luminaries grandee.

units.zh: 加兵之制，諸所供給依三品將軍。
units.en: Military add-ons followed third-rank general perquisites.
units.literal: For systems with added military authority, all provisions followed third-grade generals.

units.zh: 其餘自如舊制，終武、惠、孝懷三世。
units.en: The rest followed the old regulations through the three reigns of Wu, Hui, and Xiaohuai.
units.literal: The rest followed old regulations through the reigns of Wu, Hui, and Xiaohuai.

units.zh: 光祿大夫與卿同秩中二千石，著進賢兩梁冠，黑介幘，五時朝服，佩水蒼玉，食奉日三斛。
units.en: Splendid Luminaries ranked with ministers at middle two thousand shi, wearing the two-ridged cap, black kerchief, seasonal court dress, dark jade, and three hu daily.
units.literal: Splendid Luminaries Grandee shared ministerial rank at middle two thousand shi, wore the two-beam advanced-worth cap, black inner kerchief, five-seasons court dress, dark aquamarine jade at the belt, and a daily grain allowance of three hu.

units.zh: 太康二年，始給春賜絹五十匹，秋絹百匹，綿百斤。
units.en: From 281 they received fifty bolts of spring silk, one hundred of autumn silk, and one hundred jin of cotton.
units.literal: In the second year of Taikang spring grants of fifty bolts of silk were first given, one hundred bolts in autumn, and one hundred jin of cotton.

units.zh: 惠帝元康元年，始給菜田六頃，田騶六人，置主簿、功曹史、門亭長、門下書佐各一人。
units.en: In 291 under Emperor Hui they received six qing of kitchen gardens, six field grooms, and one each of chief clerk, merit clerk, gate chief, and household scribe.
units.literal: In the first year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui six qing of vegetable fields and six field grooms were first granted, with one chief clerk, merit clerk, gate pavilion chief, and household scribe established.

units.zh: 驃騎已下及諸大將軍不開府非持節都督者，品秩第二，其祿與特進同。
units.en: Junior martial peers without mansions or credentials ranked second with stipends like special advancement.
units.literal: Cavalry-in-Chief downward and various grand generals who did not open headquarters and were not credential-bearing commanders were grade second; their stipends matched extraordinary advancement.

units.zh: 置長史、司馬各一人，秩千石；
units.en: Each carried chief clerk and adjutant at one thousand shi;
units.literal: One chief clerk and one adjutant each at one thousand shi;

units.zh: 主簿，功曹史，門下督，錄事，兵鎧士賊曹，營軍、刺奸、帳下都督，功曹書佐門吏，門下書吏各一人。
units.en: full secretarial staff—chief clerk through gate clerks—one per slot.
units.literal: chief clerk, merit clerk, household inspector, recorder, armor office, gentlemen-thieves office, camp army, malfeasance inspector, household-area commander, merit clerk clerk assistants, gate clerks—one each.

units.zh: 其假節為都督者，所置與四征鎮加大將軍不開府為都督者同。
units.en: Credential-only commanders matched expeditionary grand generals without mansions.
units.literal: Those with borrowed credentials serving as commanders had the same staffing as expedition and garrison grand generals without headquarters serving as commanders.

units.zh: 四征鎮安平加大將軍不開府、持節都督者，品秩第二，置參佐吏卒，幕府兵騎如常都督制，唯朝會祿賜從二品將軍之例。
units.en: Expeditionary grand generals with credentials but no mansion ranked second; staffs matched normal commanders; court pay followed second-grade rules.
units.literal: Four expeditions, garrisons, pacification, peace with added grand general title, without headquarters, credential-bearing commanders were grade second; staff and runners followed ordinary commander rules; only court assembly stipends followed second-grade general precedent.

units.zh: 然則持節、都督無定員，前漢遣使始有持節。
units.en: Area commanders had no fixed headcount; Former Han invented credential-bearing missions.
units.literal: Thus credential-bearing commanders had no fixed quota; Former Han first had credential-bearing envoys.

units.zh: 光武建武初，征伐四方，始權時置督軍御史，事竟罷。
units.en: Guangwu's early campaigns used temporary army censors, then disbanded them.
units.literal: At the start of Guangwu's Jianwu, campaigning in four directions, temporary army-supervising censors were first set up; when the task ended they were abolished.

units.zh: 建安中，魏武為相，始遣大將軍督之。
units.en: Mid-Jian'an Cao Cao as chancellor began assigning grand generals to oversee armies.
units.literal: In Jian'an, Wei Wu as chancellor first dispatched grand generals to supervise.

units.zh: 二十一年，征孫權還，夏侯惇督二十六軍是也。
units.en: In 216, returning from the campaign against Sun Quan, Xiahou Dun supervised twenty-six armies; this is an instance.
units.literal: In the twenty-first year, returning from campaigning against Sun Quan, Xiahou Dun supervised twenty-six armies—this is an instance.

units.zh: 魏文帝黃初三年，始置都督諸州軍事，或領刺史。
units.en: 222 CE introduced provincial military commanders, often doubling as governors.
units.literal: In Wei Wendi's third Huangchu year, commanders-in-chief of military affairs of various provinces were first established; some concurrently held inspector posts.

units.zh: 又上軍大將軍曹真都督中外諸軍事、假黃鉞，則總統內外諸軍矣。
units.en: Cao Zhen as senior grand general with the golden axe commanded every army at court and frontier.
units.literal: Moreover Upper-army Grand General Cao Zhen commanded inner and outer armies with borrowed yellow axe—thus he commanded all armies within and without.

units.zh: 魏明帝太和四年秋，宣帝征蜀，加號大都督。
units.en: In the autumn of Emperor Ming of Wei's fourth Taihe year, Prince Xuan campaigned against Shu and added the title supreme commander.
units.literal: Autumn of Wei Mingdi's fourth Taihe year, Prince Xuan campaigned against Shu and added the title supreme commander.

units.zh: 高貴鄉公正元二年，文帝都督中外諸軍，尋加大都督。
units.en: 254 CE Sima Zhao commanded all forces, then took supreme commander.
units.literal: In Gaoguixiang Duke's second Zhenyuan year, Prince Wen commanded inner and outer armies; soon after he added supreme commander.

units.zh: 及晉受禪，都督諸軍為上，臨諸軍次之，督諸軍為下；
units.en: Jin ranked titles: commander-in-chief highest, overseer next, supervisor lowest;
units.literal: When Jin received abdication, commander-in-chief of various armies was highest, overseeing various armies next, supervising various armies lowest;

units.zh: 使持節為上，持節次之，假節為下。
units.en: Full powers ranked above ordinary credential, which ranked above borrowed.
units.literal: Bearer of full powers highest, credential-holder next, borrowed credential lowest.

units.zh: 使持節得殺二千石以下；
units.en: Full powers allowed executing officials through two-thousand-shi rank;
units.literal: Bearer of full powers could execute officials down to two thousand shi;

units.zh: 持節殺無官位人，若軍事，得與使持節同；
units.en: Ordinary credentials covered commoners; in war matched full powers;
units.literal: credential-holder could kill persons without office rank; in military matters could match bearer of full powers;

units.zh: 假節唯軍事得殺犯軍令者。
units.en: Borrowed credentials executed only military offenders.
units.literal: borrowed credential only in military affairs could kill violators of military orders.

units.zh: 江左以來，都督中外尤重，唯王導等權重者乃居之。
units.en: South of the river, supreme command rarely fell except to figures as powerful as Wang Dao.
units.literal: Since the Jiang left, commander-in-chief of inner and outer has been especially weighty; only men of heavy authority like Wang Dao have held it.

units.zh: 三品將軍秩中二千石者，著武冠，平上黑幘，五時朝服，佩水蒼玉，食奉、春秋賜綿絹、菜田、田騶如光祿大夫諸卿制。
units.en: Third-grade two-thousand-shi generals wore warrior dress and seasonal court robes with dark jade; pay and land grants matched ministers.
units.literal: Third-grade generals at salary two thousand shi wore military caps, flat-top black scarves, five-seasons court robes, dark aquamarine jade; salary, spring-autumn silk grants, vegetable fields, field runners matched splendid luminaries grandees and various ministers.

units.zh: 置長史、司馬各一人，秩千石；
units.en: Staff included chief clerk and adjutant at one thousand shi;
units.literal: One chief clerk and one adjutant each at one thousand shi;

units.zh: 主簿，功曹，門下都督，錄事，兵鎧士賊曹，營軍、刺奸吏、帳下都督，功曹書佐門吏，門下書吏各一人。
units.en: plus the full clerical roster—chief clerk through household clerks—one per position.
units.literal: registrar, merit clerk, household commander, recorder, armor-and-gentlemen-thieves offices, camp-army and malfeasance clerks, household-area commander, merit-clerk assistants and gate clerks, household clerks—one each.

units.zh: 錄尚書，案漢武時，左右曹諸吏分平尚書奏事，知樞要者始領尚書事。
units.en: Recorder of the Secretariat: under Han Wudi, left and right bureau clerks balanced memorials, and those who knew the pivot first led Secretariat affairs.
units.literal: Recorder of the Secretariat—in tradition, under Emperor Wu of Han clerks of the left and right bureaus divided and balanced Secretariat memorials; those who knew pivotal affairs first took charge of Secretariat business.

units.zh: 張安世以車騎將軍，霍光以大將軍，王鳳以大司馬，師丹以左將軍並領尚書事。
units.en: Zhang Anshi, Huo Guang, Wang Feng, and Shi Dan each held Secretariat affairs from their martial posts.
units.literal: Zhang Anshi as General of Chariots and Cavalry, Huo Guang as Grand General, Wang Feng as Grand Marshal, and Shi Dan as General of the Left all concurrently held Secretariat affairs.

units.zh: 後漢章帝乙太傅趙憙、太尉牟融並錄尚書事。
units.en: Under Emperor Zhang of Later Han, Grand Tutor Zhao Xi and Minister of War Mou Rong both recorded Secretariat affairs.
units.literal: Under Later Han Emperor Zhang, Grand Tutor Zhao Xi and Minister of War Mou Rong both recorded Secretariat affairs.

units.zh: 尚書有錄名，蓋自憙、融始，亦西京領尚書之任，猶唐虞大麓之職也。
units.en: The recorder title on the Secretariat likely began with Xi and Rong, echoing Western Han leadership and the Great Steward of antiquity.
units.literal: The Secretariat had the title of recorder—probably beginning with Xi and Rong—also the Western Capital duty of leading the Secretariat, like the Great Steward office of Tang and Yu.

units.zh: 和帝時，太尉鄧彪為太傅，錄尚書事，位上公，在三公上，漢制遂以為常，每少帝立則置太傅錄尚書事，猶古塚宰總己之義，薨輒罷之。
units.en: Under Emperor He, Deng Biao as Grand Tutor recorded Secretariat affairs above the Three Dukes; thereafter each minor emperor got such a tutor-steward until death ended the post.
units.literal: Under Emperor He, Minister of War Deng Biao became Grand Tutor and recorded Secretariat affairs, ranking as supreme duke above the Three Dukes; Han regulations then made this constant—whenever a young emperor was enthroned a Grand Tutor recording Secretariat affairs was established, like the ancient chief steward holding all strings; upon death the office was abolished.

units.zh: 自魏晉以後，亦公卿權重者為之。
units.en: Under Wei and Jin, weighty ministers held the post as well.
units.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, powerful dukes and ministers also held it.

units.zh: 尚書令，秩千石，假銅印墨綬，冠進賢兩梁冠，納言幘，五時朝服，佩水蒼玉，食奉月五十斛。
units.en: The Secretariat director drew one thousand shi, bearing a bronze seal on a black ribbon; he wore the two-ridged scholar cap and inner-court kerchief, seasonal court robes, dark jade, and fifty hu of grain each month.
units.literal: The Director of the Secretariat had salary rank one thousand shi, borrowed bronze seal with black ribbon, wore the two-beam advanced-worth cap and speaking-inner scarf, five-seasons court dress, dark aquamarine jade at the belt, and a monthly grain allowance of fifty hu.

units.zh: 受拜則策命之，以在端右故也。
units.en: Investiture came by formal edict—his seat was the premier place at the hall's right.
units.literal: Upon investiture he received a written edict of appointment, because he stood at the right head of the hall.

units.zh: 太康二年，始給賜絹，春三十匹，秋七十匹。
units.en: From 281 onward the court added silk grants—thirty bolts each spring and seventy each autumn.
units.literal: In the second year of Taikang they began granting silk—thirty bolts in spring and seventy in autumn.

units.zh: 綿七十斤。
units.en: They also issued seventy jin of cotton.
units.literal: Seventy jin of cotton.

units.zh: 元康元年，始給菜田六頃，田騶六人，立夏後不及田者，食奉一年。
units.en: From 291 vegetable plots of six qing plus six field runners applied; if fields were not assigned after summer began, the stipend was paid in cash for a full year.
units.literal: In the first year of Yuankang they began granting six qing of vegetable land and six field runners; if after the beginning of summer the land had still not been awarded, he received one year's salary instead.

units.zh: 始賈充為尚書令，以目疾表置省事吏四人，省事蓋自此始。
units.en: Jia Chong, first as director, secured four auxiliary clerks for routine paperwork—likely the origin of the 'miscellaneous clerk' post.
units.literal: When Jia Chong first became Director of the Secretariat, because of eye trouble he memorialized to appoint four clerks for miscellaneous duties—the office of miscellaneous-affairs clerk probably began here.

units.zh: 僕射，服秩印綬與令同。
units.en: Vice directors matched the director in dress, grade, seal, and ribbon.
units.literal: The vice directors had the same robes, rank, seal, and ribbon as the director.

units.zh: 案漢本置一人，至漢獻帝建安四年，以執金吾榮郃為尚書左僕射，僕射分置左右，蓋自此始。
units.en: Han began with a single vice director; in 199 Rong He of the imperial guards became the first left vice director—splitting the post into left and right starts there.
units.literal: Originally Han established only one person; in the fourth year of Jian'an under Emperor Xian, the superintendent of the guards Rong He was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat—the division into left and right vice directors began here.

units.zh: 經魏至晉，迄于江左，省置無恆，置二，則為左右僕射，或不兩置，但曰尚書僕射。
units.en: Wei and Jin kept reshuffling the posts south of the river: two seats meant left and right; a lone officer was just 'Vice Director.'
units.literal: From Wei through Jin down to the southern court, abolition and restoration were irregular; when two were set they were left and right vice directors; when both were not filled the title was simply Vice Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 令闕，則左為省主；
units.en: If the director's chair was empty, the left vice director ran the office;
units.literal: When the director was vacant, the left vice director served as head of the department;

units.zh: 若左右並闕，則置尚書僕射以主左事。
units.en: when both vice seats were empty, a single vice director stepped in to manage the left bench.
units.literal: if both left and right were vacant, a Vice Director of the Secretariat was appointed to oversee left-side affairs.

units.zh: 列曹尚書，案尚書本漢承秦置，及武帝遊宴後庭，始用宦者主中書，以司馬遷為之，中間遂罷其官，以為中書之職。
units.en: The bureau system grew from Qin and Han: Emperor Wu had eunuchs run palace drafting with Sima Qian nominally attached; later that office was folded into what became the Palace Secretariat.
units.literal: The various bureau Masters of Writing—in origin the Secretariat continued Qin under Han; when Emperor Wu feasted in the inner palace he first used eunuchs to manage the Palace Secretariat and appointed Sima Qian to it; in the middle period that office was abolished and its duties were folded into the Palace Secretariat.

units.zh: 至成帝建始四年，罷中書宦者，又置尚書五人，一人為僕射，而四人分為四曹，通掌圖書秘記章奏之事，各有其任。
units.en: In 29 BCE Chengdi dismissed the eunuch secretariat and set five Masters of Writing—one vice director plus four bureaus sharing libraries, classified documents, and memorial traffic.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Jianshi under Chengdi the Zhongshu eunuchs were abolished and five Masters of Writing were again appointed—one serving as vice director and four forming four bureaus jointly handling archives, secret records, and memorials, each with its charge.

units.zh: 其一曰常侍曹，主丞相御史公卿事。
units.en: The first desk was the Permanent Attendant Bureau—for the chancellor, censorate, and senior ministers.
units.literal: The first was called the Permanent Attendant Bureau—it handled the chancellor, the censorate, and the ranks of ministers.

units.zh: 其二曰二千石曹，主刺史郡國事。
units.en: The second was the two-thousand-shi desk—for regional inspectors and local administration.
units.literal: The second was called the Two-Thousand-Shi Bureau—it handled inspectors and commandery-kingdom affairs.

units.zh: 其三曰民曹，主吏民上書事。
units.en: The third covered popular petitions—clerks and lay memorials.
units.literal: The third was called the People Bureau—it handled clerks and commoners submitting memorials.

units.zh: 其四曰主客曹，主外國夷狄事。
units.en: The fourth handled foreigners—tribute missions and border peoples.
units.literal: The fourth was called the Host-Guest Bureau—it handled foreign tribes and barbarians.

units.zh: 後成帝又置三公曹，主斷獄，是為五曹。
units.en: Chengdi added a Three Dukes bench for trials, bringing the count to five.
units.literal: Later Chengdi also established the Three Dukes Bureau to decide criminal cases—thus there were five bureaus.

units.zh: 後漢光武以三公曹主歲盡考課諸州郡事，改常侍曹為吏部曹，主選舉祠祀事，民曹主繕修功作鹽池園苑事，客曹主護駕羌胡朝賀事，二千石曹主辭訟事，中都官曹主水火盜賊事，合為六曹。
units.en: In Later Han, Emperor Guangwu assigned year-end assessments of the provinces and commanderies to the Three Dukes bureau; selections and sacrifices to the Personnel bureau; repairs, works, salt ponds, and gardens to the People bureau; imperial escorts and Qiang-Hu court audiences to the Host-Guest bureau; lawsuits to the Two-Thousand-Shi bureau; and fires, floods, theft, and banditry in the capital offices to the Capital Officials bureau—six bureaus in all.
units.literal: Later Han Emperor Guangwu used the Three Dukes Bureau for year-end assessment of commanderies and kingdoms; changed Permanent Attendant Bureau to Personnel Bureau for selections and sacrifices; People Bureau for repairs, projects, salt pools, and parks; Host-Guest Bureau for escorting the imperial carriage and Qiang-Hu court audiences; Two-Thousand-Shi Bureau for lawsuits; Capital Officials Bureau for fire, flood, theft, and banditry—together six bureaus.

units.zh: 並令僕二人，謂之八座。
units.en: With two vice directors they formed the famed Eight Seats.
units.literal: Together with two vice directors they were called the Eight Seats.

units.zh: 尚書雖有曹名，不以為號。
units.en: Bureaus had nicknames, but ministers were not yet titled after them.
units.literal: Although Masters of Writing had bureau names, those names were not yet formal titles.

units.zh: 靈帝以侍中梁鵠為選部尚書，于此始見曹名。
units.en: Lingdi's appointment of Liang Hu as 'Selection Bureau minister' was the first titled bureau post.
units.literal: Emperor Ling appointed attendant Liang Hu as Minister of the Selection Bureau—here a bureau name first appeared in an official title.

units.zh: 及魏改選部為吏部，主選部事，又有左民、客曹、五兵、度支、凡五曹尚書、二僕射、一令為八座。
units.en: Wei renamed Selection to Personnel; People, Rites, Five Armies, and Fiscal joined—five ministers plus two vice directors and the director filled the Eight Seats.
units.literal: Wei changed Selection Bureau to Personnel Bureau for selection affairs; there were also Left People, Host-Guest, Five Armies, and Fiscal Control—in all five bureau ministers, two vice directors, and one director making the Eight Seats.

units.zh: 及晉置吏部、三公、客曹、駕部、屯田、度支六曹、而無五兵。
units.en: Jin ran six desks—Personnel, Three Dukes, Host-Guest, Chariots, Colony Fields, Fiscal—and dropped Five Armies.
units.literal: When Jin set up Personnel, Three Dukes, Host-Guest, Chariots, Colony Fields, and Fiscal Control—six bureaus—there was no Five Armies bureau.

units.zh: 咸寧二年，省駕部尚書。
units.en: 276 CE struck the chariot ministry.
units.literal: In the second year of Xianning the Chariots Minister was abolished.

units.zh: 四年，省一僕射，又置駕部尚書。
units.en: Two years later they trimmed a vice seat and brought chariots back.
units.literal: In the fourth year one vice director was cut, and the Chariots Minister was restored.

units.zh: 太康中，有吏部、殿中及五兵、田曹、度支、左民為六曹尚書，又無駕部、三公、客曹。
units.en: Around Taikang the roster was Personnel, Palace Hall, Five Armies, Fields, Fiscal, and Left People—no chariot, Three Dukes, or guest desks.
units.literal: During Taikang there were Personnel, Palace Hall, Five Armies, Fields Bureau, Fiscal Control, and Left People as six bureau ministers—again without Chariots, Three Dukes, or Host-Guest.

units.zh: 惠帝世又有右民尚書，止于六曹，不知此時省何曹也。
units.en: Huidi added Right People while staying at six desks—which office vanished is unclear.
units.literal: Under Emperor Hui a Right People Minister appeared; there were still six bureaus—which bureau was dropped then is unknown.

units.zh: 及渡江，有吏部、祠部、五兵、左民、度支五尚書。
units.en: South of the river the bench shrank to Personnel, Sacrifices, Five Armies, Left People, and Fiscal.
units.literal: After crossing the Yangzi there were Personnel, Sacrifices, Five Armies, Left People, and Fiscal Control—five ministers.

units.zh: 祠部尚書常與右僕射通職，不恆置，以右僕射攝之，若右僕射闕，則以祠部尚書攝知右事。
units.en: Sacrifices paired with the right vice seat; if that seat sat empty, the Sacrifices minister covered right-bench business.
units.literal: The Sacrifices Minister often rotated duty with the Right Vice Director—not permanently established; the Right Vice Director deputized; if the Right Vice Director was vacant the Sacrifices Minister acted for right-side affairs.

units.zh: 左右丞，自漢武帝建始四年置尚書，而便置丞四人。
units.en: When Emperor Wu of Han established the Secretariat in the fourth year of Jianshi, four assistants were immediately placed.
units.literal: The left and right assistants—since Emperor Wu established the Secretariat in the fourth year of Jian'shi, four assistants were immediately placed.

units.zh: 及光武始減其二，唯置左右丞，左右丞蓋自此始也。
units.en: Guangwu cut the four to the familiar left and right assistants.
units.literal: When Guangwu reduced them to two, only left and right assistants remained—the left and right assistants began here.

units.zh: 自此至晉不改。
units.en: Jin kept that pairing intact.
units.literal: From then through Jin it was unchanged.

units.zh: 晉左丞主台內禁令，宗廟祠祀，朝儀禮制，選用署吏，急假；
units.en: The left wing handled bans inside the tower, temple rites, protocol, clerk appointments, and leave requests;
units.literal: Under Jin the left assistant supervised inner prohibitions of the terrace, ancestral temple sacrifices, court etiquette and ritual codes, selection and appointment of clerks, and emergency leave;

units.zh: 右丞掌台內庫藏廬舍，凡諸器用之物，及廩振人租布，刑獄兵器，督錄遠道文書章表奏事。
units.en: the right wing ran storerooms and buildings, supplies, rent cloth, prisons and arms, and long-distance paperwork.
units.literal: the right assistant managed terrace treasuries and buildings, all sorts of equipment and goods, grain relief and rent cloth collections, criminal cases and weapons, and supervising transmission of distant memorials, petitions, and memorialized business.

units.zh: 八座郎初拜，皆沿漢舊制，並集都座交禮，遷職又解交焉。
units.en: New Eight Seats still exchanged bows on the central dais per Han ritual and repeated the ceremony on transfer.
units.literal: When gentlemen of the Eight Seats were first invested they followed Han precedent: all gathered at the central dais to exchange bows; on promotion they again released the exchange bows.

units.zh: 尚書郎，西漢舊置四人，以分掌尚書。
units.en: Han began with four Secretariat gentlemen splitting the workload.
units.literal: Gentlemen of the Secretariat—Western Han originally set four to divide supervision of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 其一人主匈奴單于營部，一人主羌夷吏民，一人主戶口墾田，一人主財帛委輸。
units.en: One tracked the Xiongnu court, one frontier tribes, one household and land registers, one revenue and logistics.
units.literal: One supervised the Xiongnu shanyu's camp office, one supervised Qiang and Yi clerks and people, one supervised household registers and reclamation, one supervised wealth, silk, and transport.

units.zh: 及光武分尚書為六曹之後，合置三十四人，秩四百石，並左右丞為三十六人。
units.en: Guangwu's six-bureau reform raised thirty-four gentlemen at four hundred shi, thirty-six with the assistants.
units.literal: After Guangwu divided the Secretariat into six bureaus, thirty-four were appointed together at salary four hundred shi; with left and right assistants they numbered thirty-six.

units.zh: 郎主作文書起草，更直五日於建禮門內。
units.en: They drafted paperwork on five-day rotations inside Jianli Gate.
units.literal: The gentlemen drafted documents and rotated night duty five-day shifts inside the Jianli Gate.

units.zh: 尚書郎初從三署詣台試，守尚書郎，中歲滿稱尚書郎，三年稱侍郎，選有吏能者為之。
units.en: Trainees arrived from the Three Offices, served probation, earned full gentleman status after a year and deputy rank after three—only capable men advanced.
units.literal: Gentlemen of the Secretariat first came from the Three Offices to the terrace on probation as acting gentlemen; after one year within they were called Gentlemen of the Secretariat; after three years they were called deputy gentlemen; men of administrative talent were selected.

units.zh: 至魏，尚書郎有殿中、吏部、駕部、金部、虞曹、比部、南主客、祠部、度支、庫部、農部、水部、儀曹、三公、倉部、民曹、二千石、中兵、外兵、都兵、別兵、考功、定課，凡二十三郎。
units.en: By Wei there were twenty-three Secretariat gentlemen: Palace Hall, Personnel, Chariots, Metals, Yu Bureau, Review, Southern Host-Guest, Sacrifices, Fiscal Control, Storehouse, Agriculture, Water, Rituals, Three Dukes, Granary, People, Two-Thousand-Shi, Central Army, Outer Army, Capital Army, Separate Army, Merit Assessment, and Fixed Assessment.
units.literal: By Wei, gentlemen of the Secretariat included Palace Hall, Personnel, Chariots, Metals, Yu Bureau, Comparison Bureau, Southern Host-Guest, Sacrifices, Fiscal Control, Storehouse, Agriculture, Water, Rituals Bureau, Three Dukes, Granary, People, Two-Thousand-Shi, Central Army, Outer Army, Capital Army, Separate Army, Merit Assessment, Fixed Assessment—in all twenty-three gentlemen.

units.zh: 青龍二年，尚書陳矯奏置都官、騎兵，合凡二十五郎。
units.en: In the second year of Qinglong, Minister Chen Jiao memorialized to add Capital Officials and Cavalry, making twenty-five gentlemen in all.
units.literal: In the second year of Qinglong Minister Chen Jiao memorialized to add Capital Officials and Cavalry—twenty-five gentlemen altogether.

units.zh: 每一郎缺，白試諸孝廉能結文案者五人，謹封奏其姓名以補之。
units.en: Vacancies drew sealed lists of recommended Filial-and-Incorrupt candidates who could draft.
units.literal: Whenever a gentleman post opened, they tested several recommended filial-and-incorrupt candidates who could compose documents; sealed memorials listed names for appointment.

units.zh: 及晉受命，武帝罷農部、定課，置直事、殿中、祠部、儀曹、吏部、三公、比部、金部、倉部、度支、都官、二千石、左民、右民、虞曹、屯田、起部、水部、左右主客、駕部、車部、庫部、左右中兵、左右外兵、別兵、都兵、騎兵、左右士、北主客、南主客，為三十四曹郎。
units.en: When Jin received the mandate, Emperor Wu abolished Agriculture and Fixed Assessment and established thirty-four bureau gentlemen: Duty Affairs, Palace Hall, Sacrifices, Rituals, Personnel, Three Dukes, Review, Metals, Granary, Fiscal Control, Capital Officials, Two-Thousand-Shi, Left People, Right People, Yu Bureau, Military Colonies, Works, Water, Left and Right Host-Guest, Chariots, Coach, Storehouse, Left and Right Central Army, Left and Right Outer Army, Separate Army, Capital Army, Cavalry, Left and Right Gentlemen, Northern Host-Guest, and Southern Host-Guest.
units.literal: When Jin succeeded, Emperor Wu abolished Agriculture and Fixed Assessment, added duty affairs, Palace Hall, Sacrifices, Rituals, Personnel, Three Dukes, Comparison, Metals, Granary, Fiscal Control, Capital Officials, Two-Thousand-Shi, Left People, Right People, Yu Bureau, Colony Fields, Works, Water, Left and Right Host-Guest, Chariots, Coach Bureau, Storehouse, Left and Right Central Army, Left and Right Outer Army, Separate Army, Capital Army, Cavalry, Left and Right Gentlemen, Northern Host-Guest, Southern Host-Guest—thirty-four bureau gentlemen.

units.zh: 後又置運曹，凡三十五曹，置郎二十三人，更相統攝。
units.en: They later added Transport—thirty-five desks staffed by twenty-three gentlemen with overlapping duties.
units.literal: Later Transport Bureau was added—thirty-five bureaus in all—twenty-three gentlemen appointed, overseeing one another.

units.zh: 及江左，無直事、右民、屯田、車部、別兵、都兵、騎兵、左右士、運曹十曹郎。
units.en: South of the river ten desks vanished—including transport and several army offices.
units.literal: East of the Yangzi there were no Duty Affairs, Right People, Colony Fields, Coach Bureau, Separate Army, Capital Army, Cavalry, Left and Right Gentlemen, or Transport—ten bureau gentlemen cut.

units.zh: 康穆以後，又無虞曹、二千石二郎，但有殿中、祠部、吏部、儀曹、三公、比部、金部、倉部、度支、都官、左民、起部、水部、主客、駕部、庫部、中兵、外兵十八曹郎。
units.en: After the Kang and Mu reigns, the Yu Bureau and Two-Thousand-Shi gentlemen also disappeared; only eighteen bureau gentlemen remained: Palace Hall, Sacrifices, Personnel, Rituals, Three Dukes, Review, Metals, Granary, Fiscal Control, Capital Officials, Left People, Works, Water, Host-Guest, Chariots, Storehouse, Central Army, and Outer Army.
units.literal: After the Kang and Mu reigns Yu Bureau and Two-Thousand-Shi gentlemen were also gone; only Palace Hall, Sacrifices, Personnel, Rituals, Three Dukes, Comparison, Metals, Granary, Fiscal Control, Capital Officials, Left People, Works, Water, Host-Guest, Chariots, Storehouse, Central Army, Outer Army—eighteen bureau gentlemen remained.

units.zh: 後又省主客、起部、水部，余十五曹雲。
units.en: Three more desks—guest affairs, works, water—soon disappeared, leaving fifteen.
units.literal: Later Host-Guest, Works, and Water were also cut—fifteen bureaus remained.

units.zh: 侍中，案黃帝時風後為侍中，于周為常伯之任，秦取古名置侍中，漢因之。
units.en: Palace attendants are traced to Feng Hou under the Yellow Emperor; under Zhou the duty matched the permanent steward; Qin borrowed the ancient name to establish palace attendants, and Han continued it.
units.literal: Palace attendant—in tradition Feng Hou under the Yellow Emperor was palace attendant; under Zhou it matched the permanent steward's duty; Qin borrowed the ancient name to establish palace attendant; Han continued it.

units.zh: 秦漢俱無定員，以功高者一人為僕射。
units.en: Neither dynasty capped numbers; the senior man headed them as steward.
units.literal: Qin and Han both had no fixed quota; the highest merit holder served as chief steward.

units.zh: 魏晉以來置四人，別加官者則非數。
units.en: Wei and Jin fixed four seats; extras sat outside the quota.
units.literal: Since Wei and Jin four were established; supernumerary appointees did not count toward the quota.

units.zh: 掌儐贊威儀，大駕出則次直侍中護駕，正直侍中負璽陪乘，不帶劍，餘皆騎從。
units.en: They staged ritual and guarded spectacles: rotated duty shielded the train; the 'upright' attendant carried the seal pillion without sword; others rode escort.
units.literal: They conducted ceremonies and guarded imperial dignity; on great progresses the rotated attendant on duty guarded the carriage while the upright attendant carried the seal and rode pillion without sword; the rest rode escort.

units.zh: 禦登殿，與散騎常侍對扶，侍中居左，常侍居右。
units.en: At imperial audiences they flanked the emperor with household standing attendants—attendant left, standing attendant right.
units.literal: When the emperor mounted the hall they paired with elite cavalry standing attendants to assist—the attendant stood left, the standing attendant right.

units.zh: 備切問近對，拾遺補闕。
units.en: They answered spur-of-the-moment questions and caught policy gaps.
units.literal: They stood ready for intimate questions and nearby replies, gathering oversights and patching omissions.

units.zh: 及江左哀帝興寧四年，桓溫奏省二人，後復舊。
units.en: In 366 Huan Wen briefly cut two seats; the full four returned afterward.
units.literal: East of the Yangzi, in the fourth year of Xing'ning under Emperor Ai, Huan Wen memorialized to remove two persons; later the old quota returned.

units.zh: 給事黃門侍郎，秦官也。
units.en: Yellow-gate attendant was a Qin title.
units.literal: Gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates—it was a Qin office.

units.zh: 漢已後並因之，與侍中俱管門下眾事，無員。
units.en: Han onward paired them with palace attendants for gate business without a headcount cap.
units.literal: After Han it continued; together with palace attendants they managed all gate-affairs business under no fixed quota.

units.zh: 及晉，置員四人。
units.en: Jin capped the corps at four.
units.literal: Under Jin four posts were established.

units.zh: 散騎常侍，本秦官也。
units.en: Elite cavalry standing attendant began under Qin.
units.literal: Elite cavalry standing attendant—it was originally a Qin office.

units.zh: 秦置散騎，又置中常侍，散騎騎從乘輿車後，中常侍得入禁中，皆無員，亦以為加官。
units.en: Qin ran freelance riders behind the coach and inner-chamber standing attendants—both honorific and uncapped.
units.literal: Qin established unattached cavalry and also palace standing attendants; unattached cavalry rode behind the imperial carriage; palace standing attendants could enter the forbidden quarters—both had no quota and served as supernumerary titles.

units.zh: 漢東京初，省散騎，而中常侍用宦者。
units.en: Later Han dropped freelance riders and staffed standing attendants with eunuchs.
units.literal: Early Eastern Han cut unattached cavalry and palace standing attendants used eunuchs.

units.zh: 魏文帝黃初初，置散騎，合之於中常侍，同掌規諫，不典事，貂榼插右，騎而散從，至晉不改。
units.en: At the start of Huangchu, Emperor Wen of Wei restored unattached cavalry and merged them with palace standing attendants to offer counsel without managing affairs; marten-fur bags were tucked on the right as they rode in loose escort—unchanged through Jin.
units.literal: Wei Wendi at the start of Huangchu restored unattached cavalry, merged them with palace standing attendants to jointly offer counsel without managing affairs; marten-fur bags tucked right, riding loosely escorting—unchanged through Jin.

units.zh: 及元康中，惠帝始以宦者董猛為中常侍，後遂止。
units.en: In Yuankang, Emperor Hui first made the eunuch Dong Meng a palace standing attendant; afterward the practice stopped.
units.literal: In Yuankang under Emperor Hui the eunuch Dong Meng first became palace standing attendant; afterward it stopped.

units.zh: 常為顯職。
units.en: The post stayed an honor reserved for heavyweights.
units.literal: It was normally an eminent post.

units.zh: 給事中，秦官也。
units.en: Attendant-within was another Qin survival.
units.literal: Attendant-within—it was a Qin office.

units.zh: 所加或大夫、博士、議郎，掌顧問應對，位次中常侍。
units.en: Added to ministers or scholars, they answered imperial queries—below standing attendants in rank.
units.literal: Supernumerary holders might be grandees, erudites, or deliberation gentlemen; they handled consultation and replies, ranking below palace standing attendants.

units.zh: 漢因之。
units.en: Han kept the arrangement.
units.literal: Han continued it.

units.zh: 及漢東京省，魏世復置，至晉不改。
units.en: Later Han dropped it; Wei brought it back; Jin left it alone.
units.literal: Eastern Han cut it; Wei restored it; unchanged through Jin.

units.zh: 在散騎常侍下，給事黃門侍郎上，無員。
units.en: It sat between standing attendants and Yellow Gates—again no fixed headcount.
units.literal: It ranked below elite cavalry standing attendant and above gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates; no fixed quota.

units.zh: 通直散騎常侍，案魏末散騎常侍又有在員外者。
units.en: Late Wei added general-access seats outside the regular standing-attendant quota.
units.literal: General-access elite cavalry standing attendant—under late Wei some elite cavalry standing attendants were outside the quota.

units.zh: 泰始十年，武帝使二人與散騎常侍通員直，故謂之通直散騎常侍。
units.en: 274 CE paired two officers with standing attendants on shared rotations—hence 'general-access.'
units.literal: In the tenth year of Taishi Emperor Wu made two men rotate duty jointly with elite cavalry standing attendants—therefore they were called general-access elite cavalry standing attendants.

units.zh: 江左置四人。
units.en: The southern court assigned four such posts.
units.literal: East of the Yangzi four were established.

units.zh: 員外散騎常侍，魏末置，無員。
units.en: Wei's end introduced supernumerary standing attendants outside the roster.
units.literal: Supernumerary elite cavalry standing attendant—established at end of Wei; no quota.

units.zh: 散騎侍郎四人，魏初與散騎常侍同置。
units.en: Wei founded four deputy gentlemen alongside standing attendants.
units.literal: Four elite cavalry deputy gentlemen—Wei at the outset established them together with elite cavalry standing attendants.

units.zh: 自魏至晉，散騎常侍、侍郎與侍中、黃門侍郎共平尚書奏事，江左乃罷。
units.en: From Wei through Jin, Cavalier Regular Attendants and Cavalier Attendants joined Palace Attendants and Yellow Gate Attendants in reviewing Secretariat memorials; this was abolished east of the Yangzi.
units.literal: From Wei through Jin, Cavalier Regular Attendants and Cavalier Attendants together with Palace Attendants and Yellow Gate Attendants jointly reviewed Secretariat memorials; east of the Yangzi this was abolished.

units.zh: 通直散騎侍郎四人。
units.en: Four general-access deputy gentlemen mirrored the standing-attendant rule.
units.literal: Four general-access elite cavalry deputy gentlemen.

units.zh: 初，武帝置員外散騎侍郎，及太興元年，元帝使二人與散騎侍郎通員直，故謂之通直散騎侍郎，後增為四人。
units.en: Originally Emperor Wu established supernumerary elite cavalry deputy gentlemen; in the first year of Taixing, Emperor Yuan made two men rotate jointly with the elite cavalry deputy gentlemen—hence general-access elite cavalry deputy gentlemen—later increased to four.
units.literal: Originally Emperor Wu established supernumerary elite cavalry deputy gentlemen; in the first year of Taixing Emperor Yuan made two men rotate jointly with elite cavalry deputy gentlemen—therefore they were called general-access elite cavalry deputy gentlemen; later increased to four.

units.zh: 員外散騎侍郎，武帝置，無員。
units.en: Supernumerary deputies remained honorific extras without quota.
units.literal: Supernumerary elite cavalry deputy gentlemen—Emperor Wu established them; no quota.

units.zh: 奉朝請，本不為官，無員。
units.en: 'Court attendance' was not a bureau and had no roster.
units.literal: Court-attending audience was originally not an office; there was no quota.

units.zh: 漢東京罷三公、外戚、宗室、諸侯多奉朝請。
units.en: In Eastern Han, many of the Three Dukes, imperial in-laws, imperial clansmen, and nobles held court-attending status.
units.literal: Eastern Han abolished the Three Dukes; many imperial in-laws, imperial clansmen, and nobles held court-attending status.

units.zh: 奉朝請者，奉朝會請召而已。
units.en: It meant simply joining audiences when summoned.
units.literal: Those who court-attended merely attended court assemblies and answered summons.

units.zh: 武帝亦以宗室、外戚為奉車、駙馬、騎三都尉而奉朝請焉。
units.en: Wudi likewise titled kin as chariot, chief groom, and cavalry commandants with audience privileges.
units.literal: Emperor Wu also made imperial clansmen and in-laws chariot commandants, chief groom commandants, and cavalry commandants with court-attending status.

units.zh: 元帝為晉王，以參軍為奉車都尉，掾屬為駙馬都尉，行參軍舍人為騎都尉，皆奉朝請。
units.en: As Prince of Jin, Yuan titled adjutants chariot commandants, staff chief groom commandants, and acting staff as cavalry commandants—all court-attending.
units.literal: When Emperor Yuan was Prince of Jin he made adjutants chariot commandants, staff members chief groom commandants, and acting adjutants and attendants cavalry commandants—all court-attending.

units.zh: 後罷奉車、騎二都尉，唯留駙馬都尉奉朝請。
units.en: They later dropped chariot and cavalry commandants, leaving chief groom commandants with audience rights.
units.literal: Later chariot and cavalry commandants were abolished; only chief groom commandants retained court-attending status.

units.zh: 諸尚公主者劉惔、桓溫皆為之。
units.en: Princess husbands such as Liu Tan and Huan Wen held that nominal duty.
units.literal: Those who married princesses—Liu Tan and Huan Wen both held it.

units.zh: 中書監及令，案漢武帝游宴後庭，始使宦者典事尚書，謂之中書謁者，置令、僕射。
units.en: Emperor Wu's revels spawned eunuch-run palace drafting—styled Secretariat visitors—with director and deputy.
units.literal: Palace Secretariat supervisor and director—in tradition Han Emperor Wu feasting in the inner palace first used eunuchs to manage Secretariat affairs, called Palace Secretariat visitors; director and vice director were set.

units.zh: 成帝改中書謁者令曰中謁者令，罷僕射。
units.en: Chengdi renamed the visitor director and removed the deputy.
units.literal: Chengdi changed Palace Secretariat visitor director to inner visitor director and abolished the vice director.

units.zh: 漢東京省中謁者令，而有中官謁者令，非其職也。
units.en: Later Han dropped the inner title but kept eunuch visitors—a different job.
units.literal: Eastern Han abolished inner visitor director but had inner-court visitor directors—not the same duty.

units.zh: 魏武帝為魏王，置秘書令，典尚書奏事。
units.en: Cao Cao as Wei prince created a secretary director for memorial traffic.
units.literal: Wei Emperor Wu as Prince of Wei established Secretary Director to handle Secretariat memorial business.

units.zh: 文帝黃初初改為中書，置監、令，以秘書左丞劉放為中書監，右丞孫資為中書令；
units.en: 220 CE rebranded the office: Liu Fang supervised, Sun Zi directed.
units.literal: Wendi at the start of Huangchu changed it to Palace Secretariat, establishing supervisor and director—Secretariat left assistant Liu Fang became supervisor, right assistant Sun Zi became director;

units.zh: 監、令蓋自此始也。
units.en: Those paired titles begin there.
units.literal: supervisor and director probably began here.

units.zh: 及晉因之，並置員一人。
units.en: Jin kept one supervisor and one director.
units.literal: Jin continued it, each post holding one man.

units.zh: 中書侍郎，魏黃初初，中書既置監、令，又置通事郎，次黃門郎。
units.en: Wei added general-affairs gentlemen under Yellow Gates once supervisor and director existed.
units.literal: Palace Secretariat deputy—in Wei Huangchu at start, once Secretariat supervisor and director were set, general-affairs gentlemen were also placed, ranking below Yellow Gate gentlemen.

units.zh: 黃門郎已署事過，通事乃署名。
units.en: Yellow Gates finished drafts; general-affairs countersigned.
units.literal: After Yellow Gate gentlemen finalized documents, general-affairs gentlemen signed.

units.zh: 已署，奏以入，為帝省讀，書可。
units.en: The packet then went to the throne for imperial 'approved.'
units.literal: Once signed, it was memorialized for entry; the emperor reviewed and marked approval.

units.zh: 及晉，改曰中書侍郎，員四人。
units.en: Jin renamed them Palace Secretariat deputies—four seats.
units.literal: Under Jin the name was changed to Palace Secretariat deputy; four posts.

units.zh: 中書侍郎蓋此始也。
units.en: That is the origin of the deputy title.
units.literal: Palace Secretariat deputy probably began here.

units.zh: 及江左初，改中書侍郎曰通事郎，尋復為中書侍郎。
units.en: The southern court briefly called them general-affairs gentlemen, then reverted.
units.literal: Early east of the Yangzi Palace Secretariat deputies were renamed general-affairs gentlemen; soon restored to Palace Secretariat deputy.

units.zh: 中書舍人，案晉初初置舍人、通事各一人，江左合舍人通事謂之通事舍人，掌呈奏案章。
units.en: Early Jin paired one attendant with one messenger; south of the river merged them into general-affairs attendants who carried memorial folders to the throne.
units.literal: Palace Secretariat attendants—in tradition early Jin first set one attendant and one general-affairs messenger; east of the Yangzi combined attendant and general-affairs into general-affairs attendant, handling presentation of memorials and petitions.

units.zh: 後省，而以中書侍郎一人直西省，又掌詔命。
units.en: They later folded the post; a single deputy minded the western bureau and drafted edicts.
units.literal: Later it was abolished, and one Palace Secretariat deputy rotated duty in the western bureau, also handling edicts and commands.

units.zh: 秘書監，案漢桓帝延熹二年置秘書監，後省。
units.en: Han Huan created a library director in 159 CE; the seat later vanished.
units.literal: Director of the Palace Library—in tradition Emperor Huan of Han in the second year of Yanxi established a Palace Library director; later it was cut.

units.zh: 魏武為魏王，置秘書令、丞。
units.en: Cao Cao as Wei prince named a secretary director and deputy for archives.
units.literal: Wei Emperor Wu as Prince of Wei established Palace Secretary director and assistant.

units.zh: 及文帝黃初初，置中書令，典尚書奏事，而秘書改令為監。
units.en: Huangchu split drafting from archives: Zhongshu handled memorials while the old secretary director became library supervisor.
units.literal: When Wendi at the start of Huangchu established Palace Secretariat director to manage Secretariat memorial business, the Palace Secretary director title was changed to supervisor.

units.zh: 後以何禎為秘書丞，而秘書先自有丞，乃以禎為秘書右丞。
units.en: He Zhen became library deputy while a deputy already existed—so he took the new right-deputy slot.
units.literal: Later He Zhen was appointed Palace Library assistant, but the library already had an assistant; therefore Zhen was made Right Assistant of the Palace Library.

units.zh: 及晉受命，武帝以秘書並中書省，其秘書著作之局不廢。
units.en: Wudi folded library staff into the Zhongshu apparatus but kept the historiography office alive.
units.literal: When Jin received the mandate, Emperor Wu merged the Palace Library with the Palace Secretariat bureau, yet the library composition bureau was not abolished.

units.zh: 惠帝永平中，復置秘書監，其屬官有丞，有郎，並統著作省。
units.en: Huidi revived the library supervisor with deputies and gentlemen running the composition wing.
units.literal: Under Emperor Hui in the Yongping era the Palace Library supervisor was restored; subordinate offices included assistants and gentlemen, jointly overseeing the Composition Bureau.

units.zh: 著作郎，周左史之任也。
units.en: The compiler post echoed Zhou's left historian.
units.literal: Composition gentleman—it was the duty of Zhou's left historian.

units.zh: 漢東京圖籍在東觀，故使名儒著作東觀，有其名，尚未有官。
units.en: In Eastern Han, maps and registers were kept in the Eastern Observatory, so famed scholars wrote there; the title existed in name, but not yet as an office.
units.literal: In Eastern Han, maps and registers were kept in the Eastern Observatory, so famed scholars were made to compose works in the Eastern Observatory; the name existed, but there was not yet an official post.

units.zh: 魏明帝太和中，詔置著作郎，於此始有其官，隸中書省。
units.en: Wei Mingdi minted the composition gentleman title under Zhongshu.
units.literal: Wei Mingdi in the Taihe era issued an edict establishing composition gentlemen—here it first became an office, subordinate to the Palace Secretariat.

units.zh: 及晉受命，武帝以繆徵為中書著作郎。
units.en: Wudi named Miao Zheng as Zhongshu compiler.
units.literal: When Jin received the mandate, Emperor Wu appointed Miao Zheng as Palace Secretariat composition gentleman.

units.zh: 元康二年，詔曰：「著作舊屬中書，而秘書既典文籍，今改中書著作為秘書著作。」
