units.en: In the second year of Yuankang an edict said: "Composition formerly belonged to the Palace Secretariat; since the Palace Library already manages documents, now change Palace Secretariat composition to Palace Library composition."
units.literal: In the second year of Yuankang an edict said: "Composition formerly belonged to the Palace Secretariat; since the Palace Library already manages documents, now change Palace Secretariat composition to Palace Library composition."

units.zh: 於是改隸秘書省。
units.en: Compilers henceforth answered to the library bureau.
units.literal: Thus they were reassigned to the Palace Library bureau.

units.zh: 後別自置省而猶隸秘書。
units.en: They eventually spun up a dedicated bureau still under library oversight.
units.literal: Later they separately established a bureau yet still reported to the Palace Library.

units.zh: 著作郎一人，謂之大著作郎，專掌史任，又置佐著作郎八人。
units.en: One chief compiler ran history with eight assistants.
units.literal: One composition gentleman was called senior composition gentleman, solely handling historical duty; eight assistant composition gentlemen were also appointed.

units.zh: 著作郎始到職，必撰名臣傳一人。
units.en: New compilers opened their tenure by drafting a notable minister biography.
units.literal: When composition gentlemen first took office they had to compose one biography of a celebrated minister.

units.zh: 太常、光祿勳、衛尉、太僕、廷尉、大鴻臚、宗正、大司農、少府、將作大匠、太后三卿、大長秋，皆為列卿，各置丞、功曹、主簿、五官等員。
units.en: The ranked ministers were the Minister of Ceremonies, Chamberlain for Attendants, Commandant of the Guards, Grand Coachman, Minister of Justice, Grand Herald, Director of Imperial Clan Affairs, Minister of Finance, Lesser Treasurer, Grand Artisan, the three ministers of the Empress Dowager, and the Empress's Privy Treasurer; each had assistants, merit clerks, chief clerks, and gatekeeper officers.
units.literal: Minister of Ceremonies, Chamberlain for Attendants, Commandant of the Guards, Grand Coachman, Minister of Justice, Grand Herald, Director of Imperial Clan Affairs, Minister of Finance, Lesser Treasurer, Grand Artisan, the Three Ministers of the Empress Dowager, and Privy Treasurer of the Empress—all were ranked ministers; each had assistants, merit clerks, chief clerks, gatekeeper officers, and the like.

units.zh: 太常，有博士、協律校尉員，又統太學諸博士、祭酒及太史、太廟、太樂、鼓吹、陵等令，太史又別置靈台丞。
units.en: The Minister of Ceremonies had erudites and pitch-pipe commandants, and also supervised the Imperial Academy erudites and libationer, the directors of Astrology, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Music, the drum-and-pipe bands, and the mausolea; the Astrology Office separately had a Spirit Terrace assistant.
units.literal: The Minister of Ceremonies had erudites and harmonics commandants on staff; also supervised Imperial Academy erudites and libationer, and directors for Astrology, Imperial Temple, Music, drum-and-pipe bands, mausolea—the Astrology Office additionally placed a Spirit Terrace assistant.

units.zh: 太常博士，魏官也。
units.en: Wei created the Ceremonies erudite posts.
units.literal: Minister of Ceremonies erudites were Wei offices.

units.zh: 魏文帝初置，晉因之。
units.en: Wendi founded them; Jin kept them.
units.literal: Wei Wendi first established them; Jin continued.

units.zh: 掌引導乘輿。
units.en: They escorted the sovereign's carriage.
units.literal: They guided and led the imperial carriage.

units.zh: 王公已下應追諡者，則博士議定之。
units.en: Erudites voted posthumous styles for nobles.
units.literal: For kings and dukes downward who merited posthumous epithets, the erudites deliberated and fixed them.

units.zh: 協律校尉，漢協律都尉之職也，魏杜夔為之。
units.en: The harmonics post descended from Han's pitch officer—Du Kui filled it under Wei.
units.literal: Harmonics commandant—it was the duty of Han's harmonics superintendent; Wei's Du Kui held it.

units.zh: 及晉，改為協律校尉。
units.en: Jin retitled it harmonics commandant.
units.literal: Under Jin it was changed to harmonics commandant.

units.zh: 晉初承魏制，置博士十九人。
units.en: Early Jin kept nineteen classical chairs from Wei.
units.literal: Early Jin inherited Wei regulations and established nineteen erudites.

units.zh: 及咸甯四年，武帝初立國子學，定置國子祭酒、博士各一人，助教十五人，以教生徒。
units.en: 278 CE launched the academy with one libationer, one professor, and fifteen assistants teaching disciples.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Xianning Emperor Wu first founded the Imperial Academy, fixing one libationer and one erudite each, fifteen teaching assistants, to instruct students.

units.zh: 博士皆取履行清淳，通明典義者，若散騎常侍、中書侍郎、太子中庶子以上，乃得召試。
units.en: Candidates needed pristine résumés and canonical mastery; only senior attendants and above sat the exam.
units.literal: Erudites were all drawn from men of pure conduct who mastered canonical meaning; only those ranked elite cavalry standing attendant, Palace Secretariat deputy, heir-apparent household attendant or higher could be summoned to examination.

units.zh: 及江左初，減為九人。
units.en: South of the river the corps shrank to nine chairs.
units.literal: Early east of the Yangzi it was reduced to nine.

units.zh: 元帝末，增《儀禮》、《春秋公羊》博士各一人，合為十一人。
units.en: Late Yuandi added Etiquette and Gongyang chairs—eleven professors.
units.literal: At the end of Emperor Yuan's reign one Ceremonies erudite each was added for Etiquette and Gongyang Commentary on the Spring and Autumn, totaling eleven.

units.zh: 後又增為十六人，不復分掌《五經》，而謂之太學博士也。
units.en: The roster grew to sixteen unified professors rather than one canon each.
units.literal: Later it was increased to sixteen; they no longer split custody of the Five Classics but were called Imperial Academy erudites.

units.zh: 孝武太元十年，損國子助教員為十人。
units.en: 385 CE trimmed academy assistants to ten.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowu in the tenth year of Taiyuan cut Imperial Academy assistant posts to ten.

units.zh: 光祿勳，統武賁中郎將、羽林郎將、冗從僕射、羽林左監、五官左右中郎將、東園匠、太官，禦府、守宮、黃門、掖庭、清商、華林園、暴室等令。
units.en: The Chamberlain for Attendants supervised the Huben guards, Yulin escorts, supernumerary attendants, the Yulin left intendant, the left and right Generals of the Gentlemen of the Five Offices, Eastern Park craftsmen, kitchens, wardrobes, palace maintenance, Yellow Gates, lateral courts, Qing Shang music, Hualin Garden, and detention wards.
units.literal: The Chamberlain for Attendants supervised the Huben General of the Gentlemen, Yulin Gentlemen General, supernumerary vice director, Yulin left intendant, left and right Generals of the Gentlemen of the Five Offices, Eastern Park craftsmen, imperial kitchens, wardrobe bureau, palace maintenance, Yellow Gates, lateral courts, Qing Shang music, Hualin Garden, sudden-arrest cells, and other directors.

units.zh: 哀帝興寧二年，省光祿勳，並司徒。
units.en: 364 CE folded the Chamberlain for Attendants into the Minister of Education.
units.literal: In the second year of Xing'ning under Emperor Ai the Chamberlain for Attendants was abolished and merged into the Minister of Education.

units.zh: 孝武甯康元年復置。
units.en: 373 CE revived the Chamberlain for Attendants.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowu in the first year of Ningkang restored it.

units.zh: 衛尉，統武庫、公車、衛士、諸冶等令，左右都候，南北東西督冶掾。
units.en: Guards ran armories, carriages, foundries, patrols, and regional forge desks.
units.literal: The Commandant of the Guards supervised arsenal, public carriage office, garrison commandants, various foundry directors, left and right capital patrols, and north-south-east-west foundry clerks.

units.zh: 及渡江，省衛尉。
units.en: South of the river they struck the guards commandant.
units.literal: After crossing the Yangzi the Commandant of the Guards was cut.

units.zh: 太僕，統典農、典虞都尉，典虞丞，左右中典牧都尉，車府典牧，乘黃廄、驊騮廄、龍馬廄等令。
units.en: Coachman oversaw herds, transport animals, and stable masters.
units.literal: The Minister Coachman supervised colony commandants, herd commandants and assistants, left-right-central herd commandants, chariot office herd masters, directors for bay horses, splendid bays, dragon-horse bays, and the like.

units.zh: 典牧又別置羊牧丞。
units.en: Herds added a sheep deputy.
units.literal: The herd office additionally placed a sheep-herd assistant.

units.zh: 太僕，自元帝渡江之後或省或置。
units.en: South of the river the Coachman flickered on and off.
units.literal: The Minister Coachman after Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangzi was sometimes cut, sometimes restored.

units.zh: 太僕省，故驊騮為門下之職。
units.en: Without a Coachman the splendid stable fell under gate affairs.
units.literal: When Minister Coachman was cut, therefore splendid bay belonged to gate-affairs duty.

units.zh: 廷尉，主刑法獄訟，屬官有正、監、評，並有律博士員。
units.en: Justice handled crime and trials with rectifiers, reviewers, and statute professors.
units.literal: The Minister of Justice presided over penal law and litigation; subordinates included directors rectifying, supervising, and reviewing cases, with legal erudites on staff.

units.zh: 大鴻臚，統大行、典客、園池、華林園、鉤盾等令，又有青宮列丞、鄴玄武苑丞。
units.en: The Grand Herald supervised the Grand Envoy, guest reception, imperial parks, Hualin Garden, and hook-shield offices, and also had ranked assistants of the Green Palace and assistants of Xuanwu Garden at Ye.
units.literal: The Grand Herald supervised the Grand Envoy, guest receptions, imperial parks, Hualin Garden, hook-shield offices, and other directors; there were also ranked assistants of the Green Palace and assistants of Xuanwu Garden at Ye.

units.zh: 及江左，有事則權置，無事則省。
units.en: South of the river the Herald appeared only when busy.
units.literal: East of the Yangzi it was provisionally set when needed and cut when quiet.

units.zh: 宗正，統皇族宗人圖諜，又統太醫令史，又有司牧掾員。
units.en: Clan affairs kept lineage rolls, court physicians, and pasture deputies.
units.literal: The Director of Imperial Clan Affairs supervised imperial clan registers and genealogy; also supervised imperial physicians and clerks; there were also herd clerks on staff.

units.zh: 及渡江，哀帝省並太常，太醫以給門下省。
units.en: Aidi folded Clan into Ceremonies and lent physicians to gate affairs.
units.literal: After crossing the Yangzi Emperor Ai merged it into Ceremonies; imperial physicians went to the Gate Affairs bureau.

units.zh: 大司農，統太倉、籍田、導官三令，襄國都水長，東西南北部護漕掾。
units.en: Finance ran granaries, sacred fields, milling, and canal convoys.
units.literal: The Minister of Finance supervised granary, sacred-field, and mill directors, Xiangguo water-intendant chief, and east-west-north-south grain convoy clerks.

units.zh: 及渡江，哀帝省並都水，孝武復置。
units.en: South of the river Aidi merged Finance into hydraulics; Xiaowu split them again.
units.literal: After crossing the Yangzi Emperor Ai merged it into the Water Superintendent; Emperor Xiaowu restored it.

units.zh: 少府，統材官校尉、中左右三尚方、中黃左右藏、左校、甄官、平准、奚官等令，左校坊、鄴中黃左右藏、油官等丞。
units.en: Treasury oversaw workshops, treasuries, crafts, markets, and palace industries.
units.literal: The Privy Treasurer supervised works commandant, left-center-right Upper Workshops, inner-yellow left-right treasuries, left works, pottery office, market balancer, palace artisans, and other directors; left works compound, Ye inner-yellow treasuries, oil offices, and other assistants.

units.zh: 及渡江，哀帝省並丹陽尹，孝武復置。
units.en: Aidi folded Treasury into Danyang governor; Xiaowu revived it.
units.literal: After crossing the Yangzi Emperor Ai merged it into the governor of Danyang; Emperor Xiaowu restored it.

units.zh: 自渡江唯置一尚方，又省禦府。
units.en: South of the river kept a single workshop and dropped wardrobe.
units.literal: Since crossing the Yangzi only one Upper Workshop remained; wardrobe bureau was also cut.

units.zh: 將作大匠，有事則置，無事則罷。
units.en: The palace builders appeared only for projects.
units.literal: Corps of Palace Construction was set when there was business and dismissed when idle.

units.zh: 太后三卿，衛尉、少府、太僕，漢置，皆隨太后宮為官號，在同名卿上，無太后則闕。
units.en: The Three Ministers of the Empress Dowager—Commandant of the Guards, Privy Treasurer, and Minister Coachman—were established in Han; their titles followed the empress dowager's palace, ranking above ministers of the same name, and stayed vacant when there was no empress dowager.
units.literal: The Three Ministers of the Empress Dowager—Commandant of the Guards, Privy Treasurer, Minister Coachman—Han established them; all followed the empress dowager's palace as title designations, ranking above ministers of the same name; when there was no empress dowager they stayed vacant.

units.zh: 魏改漢制，在九卿下。
units.en: Wei ranked dowager ministers under the Nine Ministers.
units.literal: Wei altered Han regulations, placing them below the Nine Ministers.

units.zh: 及晉復舊，在同號卿上。
units.en: Jin returned them above peers with identical names.
units.literal: When Jin restored the old pattern they again ranked above same-title ministers.

units.zh: 大長秋，皇后卿也，有後則置，無後則省。
units.en: The empress steward existed only when a consort reigned.
units.literal: Grand Privy Treasurer of the Empress—it was the empress's minister; established when there was an empress, cut when none.

units.zh: 御史中丞，本秦官也，秦時，御史大夫有二丞，其一御史丞，其一為中丞。
units.en: The censorate assistant director was a Qin office; the censor-in-chief had two deputies, one of them the assistant director.
units.literal: Assistant Director of the Censorate was originally a Qin office; in Qin times the Censor-in-Chief had two assistants, one censor assistant and one assistant director.

units.zh: 中丞外督部刺史，內領侍御史，受公卿奏事，舉劾案章。
units.en: Externally he oversaw regional inspectors; internally he led attendant censors, received ministerial memorials, and handled impeachments.
units.literal: The assistant director supervised regional inspectors externally and led attendant censors internally, received memorials from dukes and ministers, and impeached according to case records.

units.zh: 漢因之，及成帝綏和元年，更名御史大夫為大司空，置長史，而中丞官職如故。
units.en: Han followed this; in the first year of Suihe under Emperor Cheng (7 BCE) the Censor-in-Chief was renamed Grand Minister of Works and a chief clerk was established, while the assistant director's duties remained as before.
units.literal: Han followed this; in the first year of Suihe under Emperor Cheng the Censor-in-Chief was renamed Grand Minister of Works and a chief clerk was established, while the assistant director's duties remained as before.

units.zh: 哀帝建平二年，復為御史大夫。
units.en: Emperor Ai restored the title Censor-in-Chief in 5 BCE.
units.literal: In the second year of Jianping under Emperor Ai it was again made Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 元壽二年，又為大司空，而中丞出外為御史臺主。
units.en: In 1 BCE it reverted to Grand Minister of Works, and the assistant director headed the separate Censorate Bureau.
units.literal: In the second year of Yuanshou it again became Grand Minister of Works, and the assistant director went outside to head the Censorate Bureau.

units.zh: 歷漢東京至晉因其制，以中丞為臺主。
units.en: From Eastern Han through Jin the assistant director remained bureau head.
units.literal: Through Eastern Han at Luoyang down to Jin they followed this system, making the assistant director head of the bureau.

units.zh: 治書侍御史，案漢宣帝幸宣室齋居而決事，令侍御史二人治書侍側，後因別置，謂之治書侍御史，蓋其始也。
units.en: Han Xuan's Basilica sessions spawned side clerks who became law-editing censors.
units.literal: Law-editing attendant censor—in tradition Emperor Xuan of Han held court fasting in the Basilica and decided cases, ordering two attendant censors to edit documents at his side; afterward they were separately established—called law-editing attendant censors—probably beginning here.

units.zh: 及魏，又置治書執法，掌奏劾，而治書侍御史掌律令，二官俱置。
units.en: Wei paired jurisprudence censors with impeachment editors.
units.literal: Under Wei law-enforcement editors were also established to handle impeachment memorials while law-editing attendant censors handled statutes—both offices existed.

units.zh: 及晉，唯置治書侍御史，員四人。
units.en: Jin kept four law-editing censors only.
units.literal: Under Jin only law-editing attendant censors remained—four posts.

units.zh: 泰始四年，又置黃沙獄治書侍御史一人，秩與中丞同，掌詔獄及廷尉不當者皆治之。
units.en: 268 CE added a Yellow Sands censor equal to the assistant director for edict prisons and judicial appeal.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi another Yellow Sands prison law-editing attendant censor was added at salary matching the assistant director, handling imperial-order prisons and correcting injustice from the Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 後並河南，遂省黃沙治書侍御史。
units.en: Once Henan merged in, Yellow Sands censors vanished.
units.literal: Later when merged with Henan the Yellow Sands law-editing attendant censor was cut.

units.zh: 及太康中，又省治書侍御史二員。
units.en: Taikang trimmed two law editors.
units.literal: During Taikang two law-editing attendant censors were again cut.

units.zh: 侍御史，案二漢所掌凡有五曹：一曰令曹，掌律令；
units.en: Han censors ran five desks—statutes first;
units.literal: Attendant censors—in tradition Former and Later Han supervised five divisions: first called Statutes Division, handling statutes and ordinances;

units.zh: 二曰印曹，掌刻印；
units.en: seals second;
units.literal: second called Seals Division, handling seal carving;

units.zh: 三曰供曹，掌齋祠；
units.en: supplies third;
units.literal: third called Supplies Division, handling fasting sacrifices;

units.zh: 四曰尉馬曹，掌廄馬；
units.en: stables fourth;
units.literal: fourth called Stable Horses Division, handling stable horses;

units.zh: 五曰乘曹，掌護駕。
units.en: escort fifth.
units.literal: fifth called Riding Division, handling imperial escort.

units.zh: 魏置八人。
units.en: Wei ran eight censors.
units.literal: Wei established eight.

units.zh: 及晉，置員九人，品同治書，而有十三曹：吏曹、課第曹、直事曹、印曹、中都督曹、外都督曹、媒曹、符節曹、水曹、中壘曹、營軍曹、法曹、算曹。
units.en: Under Jin, nine posts were established at the same grade as the law-editing attendant censors, but they covered thirteen desks: Personnel, Merit Ranking, Duty Affairs, Seals, Inner Area Command, Outer Area Command, Matchmaking, Tallies, Water, Inner Rampart, Camp Army, Law, and Arithmetic.
units.literal: Under Jin nine posts were established, grade matching law editors, yet there were thirteen divisions: Personnel, Merit Ranking, Duty Affairs, Seals, Inner Area Command, Outer Area Command, Matchmaking, Tallies, Water, Inner Rampart, Camp Army, Law, Arithmetic.

units.zh: 及江左初，省課第曹，置庫曹，掌廄牧牛馬市租，後分曹，置外左庫、內左庫雲。
units.en: South of the river swapped merit rankings for storehouse desks tracking herds and rents, later splitting inner and outer vaults.
units.literal: Early east of the Yangzi Merit Ranking was cut and Storehouse added for stable herds, cattle, horses, and market rents; later the division split into outer-left and inner-left storehouses.

units.zh: 殿中侍御史，案魏蘭台遣二御史居殿中，伺察非法，即其始也。
units.en: Wei placed hall watchers from the Orchid Terrace.
units.literal: Palace hall attendant censors—in tradition Wei's Orchid Terrace dispatched two censors inside the palace hall to watch for illegality—probably beginning here.

units.zh: 及晉，置四人，江左置二人。
units.en: Jin used four hall censors; south of the river two.
units.literal: Under Jin four were established; east of the Yangzi two.

units.zh: 又案魏晉官品令又有禁防禦史第七品，孝武太元中有檢校御史吳琨，則此二職亦蘭台之職也。
units.en: Rank lists included defense and inspector censors—Wu Kun shows both stayed under the terrace.
units.literal: Moreover Wei-Jin rank regulations also listed defense censors at seventh grade; during Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan era inspector-censor Wu Kun appeared—thus both posts belonged to Orchid Terrace duties.

units.zh: 符節御史，秦符璽令之職也。
units.en: Tally censors descended from Qin's seal office.
units.literal: Tally censor—it was the duty of Qin's tally director.

units.zh: 漢因之，位次御史中丞。
units.en: Han ranked them under the assistant director.
units.literal: Han continued it, ranking below the assistant director.

units.zh: 至魏，別為一台，位次御史中丞，掌授節、銅武符、竹使符。
units.en: Wei gave tallies its own desk below the assistant director for seals and tokens.
units.literal: By Wei it became a separate bureau ranking below the assistant director, managing issuance of credentials, bronze martial tallies, and bamboo mission tallies.

units.zh: 及泰始九年，武帝省並蘭台，置符節御史掌其事焉。
units.en: 273 CE folded tally duty back into the terrace.
units.literal: In the ninth year of Taishi Emperor Wu merged it into the Orchid Terrace and established tally censors to manage those affairs.

units.zh: 司隸校尉，案漢武初置十三州，刺史各一人，又置司隸校尉，察三輔、三河、弘農七郡，曆漢東京及魏晉，其官不替。
units.en: Emperor Wu of Han first established thirteen provinces with one inspector each, and also established the Metropolitan Commandant to inspect the seven commanderies of the Three Adjuncts, the Three Rivers, and Hongnong; the office continued unchanged through Eastern Han, Wei, and Jin.
units.literal: Metropolitan Commandant—in tradition Emperor Wu of Han first established thirteen provinces with one inspector each; he also established the Metropolitan Commandant to inspect the Three Adjuncts, the Three Rivers, and Hongnong—seven commanderies. Through Eastern Han and Wei-Jin the office continued unchanged.

units.zh: 屬官有功曹、都官從事、諸曹從事、部郡從事、主簿、錄事、門下書佐、省事、記室書佐、諸曹書佐守從事、武猛從事等員，凡吏一百人，卒三十二人。
units.en: Staff topped out at one hundred clerks and thirty-two runners across myriad desks.
units.literal: Subordinate offices included merit clerk, capital clerk, various bureau clerks, commandery clerks, chief clerk, recorder, gate document clerks, miscellaneous clerks, secretary clerks, various bureau clerks including guards and clerks—in all one hundred clerks and thirty-two runners.

units.zh: 及渡江，乃罷司隸校尉官，其職乃揚州刺史也。
units.en: South of the river Yangzhou's governor absorbed metropolitan supervision.
units.literal: After crossing the Yangzi the Metropolitan Superintendent post was abolished; its duties fell to the governor of Yangzhou.

units.zh: 謁者僕射，秦官也，自漢至魏因之。
units.en: Chief usher came from Qin through Wei.
units.literal: Chief usher—it was a Qin office; from Han through Wei it continued.

units.zh: 魏置僕射，掌大拜授及百官班次，統謁者十人。
units.en: Wei's chief steward staged audiences and lineups with ten ushers.
units.literal: Wei established chief steward directing grand investitures and court seating order, supervising ten ushers.

units.zh: 及武帝省僕射，以謁者並蘭台。
units.en: Wudi merged ushers into the terrace.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu cut chief steward, ushers merged into the Orchid Terrace.

units.zh: 江左復置僕射，後又省。
units.en: South of the river restored then dropped the steward.
units.literal: East of the Yangzi chief steward was restored; later cut again.

units.zh: 都水使者，漢水衡之職也。
units.en: The water envoy continued Han's hydraulic commissioner.
units.literal: Water superintendent envoy—it was Han's superintendent of waters duty.

units.zh: 漢又有都水長丞，主陂池灌溉，保守河渠，屬太常。
units.en: Han tasked Ceremonies with dikes and canals via water intendants.
units.literal: Han also had chief and assistant water intendants managing dikes, irrigation, and river conservation under Ceremonies.

units.zh: 漢東京省都水，置河堤謁者，魏因之。
units.en: Later Han switched to dike ushers; Wei kept them.
units.literal: Eastern Han cut unified water office and placed river-dike ushers; Wei continued.

units.zh: 及武帝省水衡，置都水使者一人，以河堤謁者為都水官屬。
units.en: Wudi replaced the old water ministry with one envoy over dike officers.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu cut the superintendent of waters he established one water superintendent envoy, making river-dike ushers subordinates of water offices.

units.zh: 及江左，省河堤謁者，置謁者六人。
units.en: South of the river swapped dike ushers for six general ushers.
units.literal: East of the Yangzi river-dike ushers were cut and six ushers were placed.

units.zh: 中領軍將軍，魏官也。
units.en: Central Army Commander was a Wei creation.
units.literal: Central Army Commander General was a Wei office.

units.zh: 漢建安四年，魏武丞相府自置，及拔漢中，以曹休為中領軍。
units.en: Cao Cao's chancellor's office created it in 199; after Hanzhong fell, Cao Xiu became Central Army Commander.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Jian'an of Han, Cao Wu's chancellor's office established it on its own; after taking Hanzhong, Cao Xiu was made Central Army Commander.

units.zh: 文帝踐阼，始置領軍將軍，以曹休為之，主五校、中壘、武衛等三營。
units.en: Wendi made it a formal Army Commander post for Cao Xiu over three camps: Five Schools, Central Rampart, and Martial Guard.
units.literal: When Wendi ascended the throne he first established the Army Commander General, appointing Cao Xiu to it to command the Five Schools, Central Rampart, and Martial Guard—three camps.

units.zh: 武帝初省，使中軍將軍羊祜統二衛、前、後、左、右、驍衛等營，即領軍之任也。
units.en: Wudi briefly abolished it and had Central Army General Yang Hu command the guard camps in the commander's stead.
units.literal: At the start of Wudi's reign it was cut; the Central Army General Yang Hu was made to command the Two Guards, Front, Rear, Left, Right, and Valiant Guard camps—the Army Commander's duty.

units.zh: 懷帝永嘉中，改中軍曰中領軍。
units.en: Under Emperor Huai in the Yongjia era it became Central Army Commander again.
units.literal: Under Emperor Huai in the Yongjia era, Central Army was renamed Central Army Commander.

units.zh: 永昌元年，改曰北軍中候，尋復為領軍。
units.en: In 322 it was briefly Northern Army Commandant, then restored as Army Commander.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongchang it was changed to Central Commandant of the Northern Army, then soon restored as Army Commander.

units.zh: 成帝世，復為中候，尋復為領軍。
units.en: Under Cheng it again became Central Commandant, then Army Commander once more.
units.literal: In Emperor Cheng's reign it again became Central Commandant, then soon again Army Commander.

units.zh: 護軍將軍，案本秦護軍都尉官也。
units.en: Army Protector General derived from the Qin army-protector commandant.
units.literal: Army Protector General—in tradition this was originally the Qin Army Protector Commandant.

units.zh: 漢因之，高祖以陳平為護軍中尉，武帝復以為護軍都尉，屬大司馬。
units.en: Han kept it; Gaozu made Chen Ping protector commandant, and Wudi restored the title under the Grand Marshal.
units.literal: Han followed this; Gaozu appointed Chen Ping Army Protector Commandant, and Wudi again made it Army Protector Commandant subordinate to the Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 魏武為相，以韓浩為護軍，史渙為領軍，非漢官也。
units.en: As chancellor, Cao Cao appointed Han Hao protector and Shi Huan commander—neither a Han title.
units.literal: When Cao Wu was chancellor, Han Hao was made Army Protector and Shi Huan Army Commander—not Han offices.

units.zh: 建安十二年，改護軍為中護軍，領軍為中領軍，置長史、司馬。
units.en: In 207 protector and commander became central protector and central commander, each with chief clerk and adjutant.
units.literal: In the twelfth year of Jian'an Army Protector was changed to Central Army Protector and Army Commander to Central Army Commander, with chief clerks and adjutants established.

units.zh: 魏初，因置護軍將軍，主武官選，隸領軍，晉世則不隸也。
units.en: Early Wei added Army Protector General for military appointments under the commander; Jin severed that tie.
units.literal: At the start of Wei the Army Protector General was accordingly established to manage selection of military officers, subordinate to the Army Commander; in Jin times it was no longer subordinate.

units.zh: 元帝永昌元年，省護軍，並領軍。
units.en: In 322 Emperor Yuan merged protector into commander.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongchang under Emperor Yuan the Army Protector was cut and merged with the Army Commander.

units.zh: 明帝太寧二年，復置領、護，各領營兵。
units.en: In 324 Ming restored commander and protector, each with camp troops.
units.literal: In the second year of Taining under Emperor Ming the commander and protector were restored, each commanding camp troops.

units.zh: 江左以來，領軍不復別領營，總統二衛、驍騎、材官諸營，護軍猶別有營也。
units.en: South of the river the commander oversaw guard camps collectively while the protector kept separate camps.
units.literal: Since the move east of the Yangzi the Army Commander no longer separately commanded camps but oversaw the Two Guards, Valiant Cavalry, and Artisan camps; the Army Protector still had separate camps.

units.zh: 資重者為領軍、護軍，資輕者為中領軍、中護軍。
units.en: Senior appointees were commander and protector; junior ones central commander and central protector.
units.literal: Those of heavier standing were Army Commander and Army Protector; those of lighter standing were Central Army Commander and Central Army Protector.

units.zh: 屬官有長史、司馬、功曹、主簿、五官，受命出征則置參軍。
units.en: Staff included chief clerk, adjutant, merit clerk, chief scribe, and five officers, with campaign advisers when mobilized.
units.literal: Subordinate offices included chief clerk, adjutant, merit clerk, chief scribe, and five officers; when ordered on campaign military advisers were established.

units.zh: 左右衛將軍，案文帝初置中衛。
units.en: Wendi founded the central guard corps.
units.literal: Left and Right Guards generals—in tradition Wendi first established Central Guard.

units.zh: 及武帝受命，分為左右衛，以羊琇為左、趙序為右。
units.en: Wudi split Central Guard into left under Yang Xiu and right under Zhao Xu.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu received the mandate he divided them into Left and Right Guards, appointing Yang Xiu left and Zhao Xu right.

units.zh: 並置長史、司馬、功曹、主薄員，江左罷長史。
units.en: Each guard had full staff; south of the river dropped chief clerks.
units.literal: Chief clerk, adjutant, merit clerk, and chief scribe were both established; east of the Yangzi chief clerk was abolished.

units.zh: 驍騎將軍、遊擊將軍，並漢雜號將軍也。
units.en: Valiant cavalry and mobile corps were Han-style misc generals.
units.literal: Valiant Cavalry general and Mobile Corps general—both were Han miscellaneous-number generals.

units.zh: 魏置為中軍。
units.en: Wei folded them into the central army.
units.literal: Wei established them as central army.

units.zh: 及晉，以領、護、左右衛、驍騎、遊擊為六軍。
units.en: Jin counted directors, protectors, both guards, valiant cavalry, and mobile corps as the six armies.
units.literal: Under Jin, the Army Commander, Army Protector, Left and Right Guards, Valiant Cavalry, and Mobile Corps formed the Six Armies.

units.zh: 左右前後軍將軍，案魏明帝時有左軍，則左軍魏官也，至晉不改。
units.en: Wei Mingdi invented the left army; Jin kept the pattern.
units.literal: Left, Right, Front, Rear army generals—in tradition Wei Mingdi had a Left Army, so Left Army was a Wei office; unchanged through Jin.

units.zh: 武帝初又置前軍、右軍，泰始八年又置後軍，是為四軍。
units.en: Wudi first created front and right field armies; adding the rear in 272 completed the four.
units.literal: Emperor Wu at the beginning also established Front Army and Right Army; in the eighth year of Taishi Rear Army was again established—thus the four armies.

units.zh: 屯騎、步兵、越騎、長水、射聲等校尉，是為五校，並漢官也。
units.en: The five camps—garrison cavalry through thunderbolt—were Han units.
units.literal: Garrison Cavalry, Infantry, Crack Cavalry, Long River, and Thunderbolt Shoot commandants formed the Five Camps—all Han offices.

units.zh: 魏晉逮于江左，猶領營兵，並置司馬、功曹、主簿。
units.en: Wei-Jin camps kept soldiers with adjutants and clerks.
units.literal: From Wei-Jin down to the Jiang left they still commanded camp troops and each had adjutant, merit clerk, and chief clerk.

units.zh: 後省左軍、右軍、前軍、後軍為鎮衛軍，其左右營校尉自如舊，皆中領軍統之。
units.en: Directional armies merged into guard commands still overseen by the central colonel.
units.literal: Later Left, Right, Front, Rear armies were cut into Garrison Guard armies; left and right camp commandants followed old regulations, all commanded by the Central Colonel Director.

units.zh: 二衛始制前驅、由基、強弩為三部司馬，各置督史。
units.en: Both guards organized van guard, Youji archers, and strong crossbow divisions—each with overseers.
units.literal: The Two Guards first instituted Van, Youji, and Strong Crossbow as three divisions of adjutants, each with supervising clerks.

units.zh: 左衛，熊渠武賁；
units.en: The left guard drew Bear-Gully royal guards;
units.literal: Left Guard—Xiongqu tiger-ben;

units.zh: 右衛，佽飛武賁。
units.en: the right guard drew Feiyi swimmers.
units.literal: Right Guard—Cifei tiger-ben.

units.zh: 二衛各五部督。
units.en: Each guard deployed five division overseers.
units.literal: The Two Guards each had five division supervisors.

units.zh: 其命中武賁，驍騎、遊擊各領之。
units.en: Crack-shot guards answered to valiant cavalry and mobile corps.
units.literal: As for accurate-shot tiger-ben, Valiant Cavalry and Mobile Corps each commanded them.

units.zh: 又置武賁、羽林、上騎、異力四部，並命中為五督。
units.en: Tiger guards, feathered forest, elite riders, and picked strongmen joined crack shots as five commands.
units.literal: Tiger-ben, feathered forest, superior cavalry, and extraordinary strength formed four divisions; together with accurate-shot they made five supervised divisions.

units.zh: 其衛、鎮四軍如五校，各置千人。
units.en: Guard and field armies mirrored the five camps at one thousand troops each.
units.literal: The Guard and Garrison four armies matched the Five Camps—each established one thousand men.

units.zh: 更制殿中將軍，中郎、校尉、司馬比驍騎。
units.en: Hall generals, palace gentlemen, and camp officers matched valiant-cavalry grade.
units.literal: Palace hall generals were reformed; gentlemen-of-the-palace, commandants, and adjutants ranked alongside Valiant Cavalry.

units.zh: 持椎斧武賁，分屬二衛。
units.en: Ax-wielding tiger guards split between both guards.
units.literal: Mace-and-axe tiger-ben were divided between the Two Guards.

units.zh: 尉中武賁、持鈒冗從、羽林司馬，常從人數各有差。
units.en: Hall guards, axe escorts, and feathered-forest adjutants carried differing standing complements.
units.literal: Palace tiger-ben, dagger-axe supernumerary followers, feathered-forest adjutants—regular escort complements varied by detail.

units.zh: 武帝甚重兵官，故軍校多選朝廷清望之士居之。
units.en: Wudi prized martial appointments and stacked camps with respected courtiers.
units.literal: Emperor Wu greatly esteemed military officers; therefore army-school posts often selected eminent worthies from court.

units.zh: 先是，陳勰為文帝所待，特有才用，明解軍令。
units.en: Chen Xie enjoyed Wendi's favor—acute on army regulations.
units.literal: Earlier Chen Xie had been favored by Emperor Wen, unusually talented and skilled, clearly understanding military regulations.

units.zh: 帝為晉王，委任使典兵事。
units.en: When the emperor was Prince of Jin, he entrusted him to manage military affairs.
units.literal: When the emperor was Prince of Jin he entrusted him to manage military affairs.

units.zh: 及蜀破後，令勰受諸葛亮圍陣用兵倚伏之法，又甲乙校標幟之制，勰悉暗練之，遂以勰為殿中典兵中郎將，遷將軍。
units.en: After Shu fell he ordered Xie to receive Zhuge Liang's encirclement formations and the hidden methods of maneuver and ambush, as well as the first-and-second camp banner system; Xie practiced them all to mastery and was therefore made palace hall gentleman commanding troops, later promoted general.
units.literal: After Shu fell he ordered Xie to receive Zhuge Liang's encirclement formations and methods of troop maneuvers and ambush, as well as the first-and-second camp banner system; Xie practiced them all to fluency; therefore Xie was made palace hall gentleman commanding troops, later promoted general.

units.zh: 久之，武帝每出入，勰持白獸幡在乘輿左右，鹵簿陳列齊肅。
units.en: For years Chen Xie bore the white beast banner beside the coach—his drills stayed razor sharp.
units.literal: After a long time, whenever Emperor Wu went out Xie held the white beast banner beside the imperial carriage; the guard of honor arrayed itself perfectly solemn.

units.zh: 太康末，武帝嘗出射雉，勰時已為都水使者，散從。
units.en: Late Taikang Wudi hunted pheasants while Chen Xie, now water envoy, tagged along.
units.literal: Near the end of Taikang Emperor Wu once went out to shoot pheasants; Xie by then was water superintendent envoy, following loosely.

units.zh: 車駕逼暗乃還，漏已盡，當合函，停乘輿，良久不得合，乃詔勰合之。
units.en: The carriage turned back only when dusk pressed close; the clepsydra had run out, and the armored coach-box should have been closed; they halted the imperial carriage and long could not close it, so an edict ordered Xie to close it.
units.literal: The carriage turned back only when dusk pressed close; the clepsydra had run out—it should have closed the armored coach-box; they halted the imperial carriage; long unable to close it—thereupon an edict ordered Xie to close it.

units.zh: 勰舉白獸幡指麾，須臾之間而函成。
units.en: He waved the banner and snapped the coach shell shut.
units.literal: Xie raised the white beast banner and directed; in an instant the coach-box was closed.

units.zh: 皆謝勰閑解，甚為武帝所任。
units.en: Onlookers praised his practiced hand; Wudi relied on him heavily.
units.literal: All thanked Xie for his practiced skill; he was greatly trusted by Emperor Wu.

units.zh: 太子太傅、少傅，皆古官也。
units.en: Heir tutors were classical posts.
units.literal: Grand tutor and junior tutor of the heir apparent—both were ancient offices.

units.zh: 泰始三年，武帝始建官，各置一人，尚未置詹事，官事無大小，皆由二傅，並有功曹、主簿、五官。
units.en: In the third year of Taishi (267), Emperor Wu first created these offices, one post each; before any household supervisor was appointed, all business, large or small, passed through the two tutors, who also had merit clerks, chief clerks, and gatekeeper officers.
units.literal: In the third year of Taishi Emperor Wu first established the offices, each one post; not yet appointing a household supervisor—office business large or small all passed through the two tutors, who also had merit clerks, chief clerks, and gatekeeper officers.

units.zh: 太傅中二千石，少傅二千石。
units.en: Senior tutor drew near two thousand shi; junior tutor two thousand.
units.literal: Grand tutor at salary comparable to two thousand shi; junior tutor at two thousand shi.

units.zh: 其訓導者，太傅在前，少傅在後。
units.en: Instruction lined up senior tutor forward, junior aft.
units.literal: Those who instructed—grand tutor in front, junior tutor behind.

units.zh: 皇太子先拜，諸傅然後答之。
units.en: The crown prince bowed first; tutors returned the courtesy.
units.literal: The imperial heir first bowed; the tutors then answered.

units.zh: 武帝后以儲副體尊，遂命諸公居之；
units.en: Once the heir's rank swelled, grandees filled those chairs;
units.literal: Later Emperor Wu because the heir's station was august ordered various dukes to occupy the posts;

units.zh: 以本位重，故或行或領。
units.en: weight meant some served full-time, some doubled other posts.
units.literal: because the posts were weighty, therefore some served in person and some held concurrent titles.

units.zh: 時侍中任愷，武帝所親敬，復使領之，蓋一時之制也。
units.en: Ren Kai briefly doubled duty—a court expedient.
units.literal: At the time attendant Ren Kai, whom Emperor Wu personally favored and respected, was also made to oversee them—probably an arrangement of the moment.

units.zh: 咸甯元年，以給事黃門侍郎楊珧為詹事，掌宮事，二傅不復領官屬。
units.en: 275 CE Yang Yao became household supervisor so tutors shed staff.
units.literal: In the first year of Xianning gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates Yang Yao was made household supervisor handling palace business; the two tutors no longer supervised subordinates.

units.zh: 及楊珧為衛將軍，領少傅，省詹事，遂崇廣傅訓，命太尉賈充領太保，司空齊王攸領太傅，所置吏屬復如舊。
units.en: When Yang Yao became General of the Guards and concurrently Junior Tutor, the household supervisor was abolished and tutor instruction was expanded: Grand Commandant Jia Chong was ordered to serve concurrently as Grand Guardian, and Minister of Works Prince You of Qi as Grand Tutor; the appointed clerical staff returned to the old pattern.
units.literal: When Yang Yao became General of the Guards and concurrently Junior Tutor, the household supervisor was abolished; tutor instruction was then enlarged—Grand Commandant Jia Chong was ordered to serve concurrently as Grand Guardian, and Minister of Works Prince You of Qi as Grand Tutor; the appointed clerical staff returned as before.

units.zh: 二傅進賢兩梁冠，黑介幘，五時朝服，佩水蒼玉，食奉日三斛。
units.en: Tutors wore two-ridged caps, black kerchiefs, seasonal robes, jade, three hu daily.
units.literal: The two tutors wore two-beam advanced-worth caps, black scarves, five-seasons court dress, dark aquamarine jade, daily grain allowance three hu.

units.zh: 太康二年，始給春賜絹五十匹，秋絹百匹，綿百斤。
units.en: 281 CE added seasonal silk and cotton allotments.
units.literal: In the second year of Taikang they began granting spring silk fifty bolts, autumn silk one hundred bolts, cotton one hundred jin.

units.zh: 其後太尉汝南王亮、車騎將軍楊駿、司空衛瓘、石鑒皆領傅保，猶不置詹事，以終武帝之世。
units.en: Afterward, the Grand Commandant Prince Liang of Runan, General of Chariots and Cavalry Yang Jun, Minister of Works Wei Guan, and Shi Jian all concurrently held tutor-guardian posts, but no household supervisor was appointed through the end of Emperor Wu's reign.
units.literal: Afterward Grand Commandant Prince Liang of Runan, General of Chariots and Cavalry Yang Jun, Minister of Works Wei Guan, and Shi Jian all held tutor-guardian posts; still no household supervisor was appointed through Emperor Wu's reign.

units.zh: 惠帝元康元年，復置詹事，二傅給菜田六頃，田騶六人，立夏後不及田者，食奉一年。
units.en: 291 CE revived the supervisor and granted tutors vegetable plots like ministers.
units.literal: Emperor Hui in the first year of Yuankang restored household supervisor; the two tutors received six qing vegetable land and six field runners; if after beginning of summer land had not been awarded, one year's salary instead.

units.zh: 置丞一人，秩千石；
units.en: One deputy at one thousand shi;
units.literal: One assistant was placed at rank one thousand shi;

units.zh: 主簿、五官掾、功曹史、主記門下史、錄事、戶曹法曹倉曹賊曹功曹書佐、門下亭長、門下書佐、省事各一人，給赤耳安車一乘。
units.en: full tutor household staff plus a red-eared carriage.
units.literal: chief clerk, gatekeeper officers, merit clerk, chief recorder, gate clerks, recorder, household office, law office, granary office, thieves office, merit clerk assistants, gate precinct chief, gate document clerks, miscellaneous clerks—one each; one red-eared secure carriage granted.

units.zh: 及湣懷建官，乃置六傅，三太、三少，以景帝諱師，故改太師為太保，通省尚書事，詹事文書關由六傅。
units.en: Minhuai's six tutors—taboo turned instructor into guardian—shared Secretariat oversight.
units.literal: When Crown Prince Minhuai established offices, six tutors were set—three senior and three junior—because of the taboo on Emperor Jing's name Shi, therefore Grand Instructor was changed to senior guardian, jointly overseeing Secretariat business; household paperwork passed through all six tutors.

units.zh: 然自元康之後，諸傅或二或三，或四或六，及永康中復不置詹事也。
units.en: Tutor counts fluctuated; Yongkang dropped the supervisor again.
units.literal: Yet from Yuankang onward tutors numbered two, three, four, or six; by Yongkang household supervisor was again absent.

units.zh: 自太安已來置詹事，終孝懷之世。
units.en: Tai'an forward kept supervisors through the prince's fall.
units.literal: From Tai'an onward household supervisor was set through Emperor Xiaohuai's reign.

units.zh: 渡江之後，有太傅少傅，不立師保。
units.en: South of the river kept grand and junior tutors only.
units.literal: After crossing the Yangzi there were grand and junior tutors but no instructor or guardian titles.

units.zh: 中庶子四人，職如侍中。
units.en: Four inner household attendants matched palace attendants.
units.literal: Four household attendants—duty like palace attendants.

units.zh: 中舍人四人，咸寧四年置，以舍人才學美者為之，與中庶子共掌文翰，職如黃門侍郎，在中庶子下，洗馬上。
units.en: In Xianning 4 (278), four Central Gentlemen were established, filled by gentlemen of fine literary talent; together with the Central Household Attendants they managed documents, with duties like Yellow Gate gentlemen, ranked below the Central Household Attendants and above the Xima.
units.literal: Four Central Gentlemen—established in the fourth year of Xianning; men of fine literary talent among the gentlemen held them; together with the Central Household Attendants they managed documents—their duty was like Yellow Gate gentlemen, below Central Household Attendants and above Xima.

units.zh: 食官令一人，職如太官令。
units.en: One food steward like the imperial chef.
units.literal: One victualing director—duty like imperial kitchen director.

units.zh: 庶子四人，職比散騎常侍、中書監令。
units.en: Four gentlemen matched standing attendants or Zhongshu leaders.
units.literal: Four gentlemen—duty comparable to elite cavalry standing attendant and Palace Secretariat supervisor or director.

units.zh: 舍人十六人，職比散騎、中書等侍郎。
units.en: Sixteen gentlemen equaled deputy-tier posts.
units.literal: Sixteen gentlemen—duty comparable to elite cavalry and Zhongshu deputies.

units.zh: 洗馬八人，職如謁者秘書，掌圖籍。
units.en: Eight grooms handled archives like secretariat ushers.
units.literal: Eight grooms—duty like ushers and secretaries, managing maps and registers.

units.zh: 釋奠講經則掌其事，出則直者前驅，導威儀。
units.en: They staged classics ceremonies and led processions when the heir traveled.
units.literal: For libation rites and lecturing on classics they managed the event; when going out the duty man rode vanguard guiding ceremony.

units.zh: 率更令，主宮殿門戶及賞罰事，職如光祿勳、衛尉。
units.en: The pitch director watched gates and discipline like Coachman and Guards.
units.literal: Pitch-pipe director—managed palace gates and rewards or punishments—duty like Imperial Coachman and Commandant of the Guards.

units.zh: 家令，主刑獄、穀貨、飲食，職比司農、少府。
units.en: The steward ran justice and pantry like Finance and Treasury.
units.literal: Household steward—managed criminal cases, grain and goods, food and drink—duty comparable to Minister of Finance and Privy Treasurer.

units.zh: 漢東京主食官令，食官令及晉自為官，不復屬家令。
units.en: Later Han tied food to the steward; Jin detached the kitchen office.
units.literal: Eastern Han took household victualing director as chief; victualing director under Jin became its own office, no longer under household steward.

units.zh: 僕，主車馬、親族，職如太僕、宗正。
units.en: The assistant handled transport and kin like Coachman and Clan director.
units.literal: Steward assistant—managed chariots, horses, and kin—duty like Minister Coachman and Director of Imperial Clan Affairs.

units.zh: 左右衛率，案武帝建東宮，置衛率，初曰中衛率。
units.en: The Left and Right Guard Rates: when Wudi built the Eastern Palace he established guard rates, first called the Central Guard Rate.
units.literal: Left and Right Guard rates—when Emperor Wu built the Eastern Palace he set guard rates, first called Central Guard Rate.

units.zh: 泰始五年，分為左右，各領一軍。
units.en: 269 CE split them into left and right armies.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Taishi they were divided into left and right, each commanding one army.

units.zh: 惠帝時，湣懷太子在東宮，又加前後二率。
units.en: Huidi's heir added front and rear guard commands.
units.literal: Under Emperor Hui Crown Prince Minhuai in the Eastern Palace added front and rear rates.

units.zh: 及江左，省前後二率，孝武太元中又置。
units.en: South of the river dropped front/rear until Taiyuan.
units.literal: East of the Yangzi front and rear were cut; Emperor Xiaowu in Taiyuan restored them.

units.zh: 王置師、友、文學各一人，景帝諱，故改師為傅。
units.en: Princes gained tutor, friend, and scholar—'instructor' became 'tutor' for taboo.
units.literal: Princes set instructor, companion, and scholar—one each; because of Emperor Jing's taboo instructor was changed to tutor.

units.zh: 友者因文王、仲尼四友之名號。
units.en: The 'friend' title echoed Confucius's four companions.
units.literal: Companion takes the name from King Wen and Confucius's four companions.

units.zh: 改太守為內史，省相及僕。
units.en: Governors became interior stewards; chancellor and assistant dropped.
units.literal: Governors were changed to interior stewards; chancellor and steward assistant were cut.

units.zh: 有郎中令、中尉、大農為三卿。
units.en: Three minister slots: intendant, commandant, grand agronomist.
units.literal: Palace intendant, commandant, and grand agronomist formed three ministers.

units.zh: 大國置左右常侍各一人，省郎中，置侍郎二人，典書、典祠、典衛、學官令、典書丞各一人，治書四人，中尉司馬、世子庶子、陵廟牧長各一人，謁者四人，中大夫六人，舍人十人，典府各一人。
units.en: Large principalities had one left and one right permanent attendant, abolished palace gentlemen, and appointed two attendants; they also had one each of the document, sacrifices, guards, academy, and document-assistant offices, four document clerks, one each of commandant marshal, heir's gentleman, and mausoleum-pasture chief, four ushers, six central grandees, ten gentlemen, and one treasury steward.
units.literal: Large principalities set left and right permanent attendants one each; palace gentlemen were abolished and two attendants appointed; document, sacrifices, guards, academy director, and document-assistant offices one each; document clerks four; commandant marshal, heir's gentleman, and mausoleum-pasture chief one each; ushers four, central grandees six, gentlemen ten, treasury stewards one each.

units.zh: 咸甯三年，衛將軍楊珧與中書監荀勖以齊王攸有時望，懼惠帝有後難，因追故司空裴秀立五等封建之旨，從容共陳時宜於武帝，以為「古者建侯，所以籓衛王室。
units.en: In the third year of Xianning, Guards General Yang Yao and Palace Secretariat supervisor Xun Xu, because Prince You of Qi enjoyed timely prestige and they feared later troubles for Emperor Hui, cited former Minister of Works Pei Xiu's five-grade feudal intent and calmly presented contemporary policy to Emperor Wu, saying: "In antiquity establishing nobility was to screen and guard the royal house.
units.literal: In the third year of Xianning Guards General Yang Yao and Palace Secretariat supervisor Xun Xu, because Prince You of Qi enjoyed timely prestige and feared later troubles for Emperor Hui, following former Minister of Works Pei Xiu's intent to establish five-grade feudal ranks, calmly presented contemporary policy to Emperor Wu, saying "In antiquity establishing nobility was to screen and guard the royal house.

units.zh: 今吳寇未殄，方岳任大，而諸王為帥，都督封國，既各不臣其統內，於事重非宜。
units.en: They argued Wu remained and princes commanding regions refused to treat staff as subjects.
units.literal: Now Wu bandits are not yet destroyed; regional posts are weighty; yet various princes serve as commanders, supervising fiefs—each not treating subordinates within his command as subjects—in affairs this is seriously inappropriate.

units.zh: 又異姓諸將居邊，宜參以親戚，而諸王公皆在京都，非扞城之義，萬世之固」。
units.en: Moreover various generals of other surnames hold the frontierlands—it is fitting to mix in kin; yet various princes and dukes all remain in the capital—not the meaning of defending walls or enduring fortification."
units.literal: Moreover various generals of other surnames hold the frontierlands—it is fitting to mix in kin; yet various princes and dukes all remain in the capital—not the meaning of defending walls or enduring fortification."

units.zh: 帝初未之察，於是下詔議其制。
units.en: Wudi ordered debate before deciding.
units.literal: The emperor at first did not examine it carefully; thereupon issued an edict ordering deliberation on the system.

units.zh: 有司奏，從諸王公更制戶邑，皆中尉領兵。
units.en: Bureaus wanted princes refitted with armed middle commandants.
units.literal: Responsible offices memorialized: follow various princes and dukes in revising household registrations—all middle commandants leading troops.

units.zh: 其平原、汝南、琅邪、扶風、齊為大國，梁、趙、樂安、燕、安平、義陽為次國，其餘為小國，皆制所近縣益滿萬戶。
units.en: Pingyuan, Runan, Langya, Fufeng, and Qi were large principalities; Liang, Zhao, Le'an, Yan, Anping, and Yiyang were middling principalities; the rest were small, with nearby counties assigned to fill each to ten thousand households.
units.literal: Pingyuan, Runan, Langya, Fufeng, and Qi were large principalities; Liang, Zhao, Le'an, Yan, Anping, and Yiyang were middling principalities; the rest were small principalities. In each case, nearby counties were assigned to bring them up to ten thousand households.

units.zh: 又為郡公制度如小國王，亦中尉領兵。
units.en: County dukes mirrored small princes with armed commandants.
units.literal: Also for commandery-duke institutions like small princes—also middle commandants leading troops.

units.zh: 郡侯如不滿五千戶王，置一軍一千一百人，亦中尉領之。
units.en: Smaller marquisates raised eleven hundred men under middle commandants.
units.literal: Commandery marquis if not reaching five thousand households like a prince—establish one army eleven hundred men—also middle commandant leading.

units.zh: 于時，唯特增魯公國戶邑，追進封故司空博陵公王沈為郡公，钜平侯羊祜為南城郡侯。
units.en: Only the Lu ducal fief had its households specially increased; former Minister of Works Duke of Boling Wang Shen was advanced to commandery duke, and Marquis of Juping Yang Hu to commandery marquis of Nancheng.
units.literal: At that time only Lu duke's registers were specially increased; posthumously advanced former Minister of Works Prince Boling Wang Shen to commandery duke; Julping marquis Yang Hu to southern-city commandery marquis.

units.zh: 又南宮王承、隨王萬各於泰始中封為縣王，邑千戶，至是改正縣王增邑為三千戶。
units.en: Taishi county princes jumped to three thousand households.
units.literal: Also Prince Cheng of Nangong and Prince Wan of Sui had been made county princes in Taishi at one thousand households—now corrected county princes augmented households to three thousand.

units.zh: 制度如郡侯，亦置一軍。
units.en: County princes matched county marquis armies.
units.literal: Institutions like commandery marquis—also establishing one army.

units.zh: 自此非皇子不得為王，而諸王之支庶，皆皇家之近屬至親，亦各以土推恩受封。
units.en: Only imperial sons could be kings; cadets took descending noble ranks.
units.literal: From this non-imperial sons could not be kings; yet various princes' lesser sons—all nearest imperial kin—each received fiefs by graded kindness.

units.zh: 其大國次國始封王之支子為公，承封王之支子為侯，繼承封王之支子為伯。
units.en: Cadet ranks stepped down duke-marquis-earl by lineage tier.
units.literal: Large and middling principalities' first enfeoffed sons of kings became dukes; heirs of enfeoffed kings' sons became marquis; successors of heirs' sons became earls.

units.zh: 小國五千戶已上，始封王之支子為子，不滿五千戶始封王之支子及始封公侯之支子皆為男，非此皆不得封。
units.en: Small-fief cadets became viscounts or barons under household thresholds.
units.literal: Small principalities above five thousand households—first enfeoffed sons of kings became viscounts; below five thousand households first enfeoffed sons of kings and first enfeoffed sons of dukes and marquis all became barons—otherwise none could be enfeoffed.

units.zh: 其公之制度如五千戶國，侯之制度如不滿五千戶國，亦置一軍千人，中尉領之，伯子男以下各有差而不置軍。
units.en: High nobles kept armies; lowest ranks had none.
units.literal: Duke institutions matched five-thousand-household principalities; marquis institutions matched sub-five-thousand principalities—also one army one thousand men led by middle commandant; earl, viscount, baron downward each graded downward without establishing armies.

units.zh: 大國始封之孫罷下軍，曾孫又罷上軍，次國始封子孫亦罷下軍，其餘皆以一軍為常。
units.en: Succession trimmed armies generation by generation.
units.literal: Large principalities' first-enfeoffed grandsons abolished lower army; great-grandsons again abolished upper army; middling principalities' first-enfeoffed descendants also abolished lower army; the rest kept one army as norm.

units.zh: 大國中軍二千人，上下軍各千五百人，次國上軍二千人，下軍千人。
units.en: Troop floors matched principality tier.
units.literal: Large principalities central army two thousand; upper and lower armies fifteen hundred each; middling principalities upper army two thousand; lower army one thousand.

units.zh: 其未之國者，大國置守土百人，次國八十人，小國六十人，郡侯縣公亦如小國制度。
units.en: Princes still in capital kept reduced household guards by size.
units.literal: Those not yet gone to fiefs—large principalities set one hundred homeland guards; middling eighty; small sixty; commandery marquis and county duke matched small principality institutions.

units.zh: 既行，所增徙各如本奏遣就國，而諸公皆戀京師，涕泣而去。
units.en: Once implemented, those whose fiefs had been augmented were sent to their domains as originally memorialized, yet the dukes clung to the capital and departed weeping.
units.literal: Once implemented, augmented relocations each as originally memorialized were dispatched to fiefs—yet various dukes all clung to the capital, weeping as they departed.

units.zh: 及吳平後，齊王攸遂之國。
units.en: After Wu fell Sima You finally left for his domain.
units.literal: After Wu was pacified Prince You of Qi then went to his fief.

units.zh: 中朝制，典書令在常侍下，侍郎上。
units.en: Capital ranks placed classics director between attendant and gentleman.
units.literal: Central court regulations—classics director ranked below standing attendant, above gentleman.

units.zh: 及渡江，則侍郎次常侍，而典書令居三軍下。
units.en: South of the river reshuffled—gentlemen under attendants, classics director under three-armies.
units.literal: East of the Yangzi gentlemen ranked below standing attendant while classics director sat below the Three Armies office.

units.zh: 公國則無中尉、常侍、三軍，侯國又無大農、侍郎，伯子男唯典書以下，又無學官、令史職，皆以次損焉。
units.en: Ducal states lacked commandants, permanent attendants, and the Three Armies; marquis states also lacked grand agronomists and attendants; earls, viscounts, and barons had only document stewards and lower offices, with no academy officers or clerks, each grade reduced in turn.
units.literal: Ducal states had no commandant, permanent attendants, or Three Armies; marquis states further had no grand agronomist or attendants; earls, viscounts, and barons had only document stewards and below, and also had no academy officers or clerks—all were reduced by rank in sequence.

units.zh: 公侯以下置官屬，隨國大小無定制，其餘官司各有差。
units.en: Staffing scaled loosely by fief.
units.literal: Dukes and marquis downward placed officials according to fief size without fixed pattern; remaining offices each differed.

units.zh: 名山大澤不以封，鹽鐵金銀銅錫，始平之竹園，別都宮室園囿，皆不為屬國。
units.en: Strategic lands and mints stayed imperial.
units.literal: Famous mountains and great marshes were not granted as fiefs; salt, iron, gold, silver, copper, tin, bamboo gardens at Shiping, detached-capital palaces and parks—none became dependent principalities.

units.zh: 其仕在天朝者，與之國同，皆自選其文武官。
units.en: Capital nobles picked staff like those in the provinces.
units.literal: Those serving in the celestial court matched those in fiefs—all chose their own civil and military officers.

units.zh: 諸入作卿士而其世子年已壯者，皆遣蒞國。
units.en: Adult heirs had to take seats in their domains.
units.literal: Various men appointed capital ministers whose heir sons were already adult—all were sent to oversee fiefs.

units.zh: 其王公已下，茅社符璽，車旗命服，一如泰始初故事。
units.en: Noble regalia matched Taishi inaugural rules.
units.literal: From dukes downward—thatched altars, tallies and seals, carriage banners and mandated dress—all followed Taishi founding precedent.

units.zh: 州置刺史，別駕、治中從事、諸曹從事等員。
units.en: Each province ran inspectors with aides and bureau staff.
units.literal: Provinces set inspectors, aide-de-camp, administrative clerks, various bureau clerks, and the like.

units.zh: 所領中郡以上及江陽、硃提郡，郡各置部從事一人，小郡亦置一人。
units.en: Interior commanderies gained division clerks.
units.literal: Among commanded interior commanderies upward plus Jiangyang and Zhuti commanderies—each commandery placed one division clerk; small commanderies also placed one.

units.zh: 又有主簿，門亭長、錄事、記室書佐、諸曹佐、守從事、武猛從事等。
units.en: Plus clerks, recorders, and bailiffs.
units.literal: Also chief clerk, gate precinct chief, recorder, secretary clerks, various bureau assistants, guard clerks, fierce clerks, and the like.

units.zh: 凡吏四十一人，卒二十人。
units.en: Forty-one clerks and twenty runners standard.
units.literal: In all forty-one clerks and twenty runners.

units.zh: 諸州邊遠，或有山險，濱近寇賊羌夷者，又置弓馬從事五十餘人。
units.en: Frontier provinces added mounted archer aides.
units.literal: Various provinces far away or with mountain hazards or bordering bandits, Qiang, and Yi—also placed fifty-some bow-and-horse clerks.

units.zh: 徐州又置淮海，涼州置河津，諸州置都水從事各一人。
units.en: Xuzhou took Huaihai aides; Liangzhou river crossing; others water clerks.
units.literal: Xuzhou additionally set Huaihai; Liangzhou set river-ford; various provinces each set one water-affairs clerk.

units.zh: 涼、益州置吏八十五人，卒二十人。
units.en: Liang and Yi ran eighty-five clerks.
units.literal: Liang and Yi provinces placed eighty-five clerks and twenty runners.

units.zh: 荊州又置監佃督一人。
units.en: Jingzhou added a colony superintendent.
units.literal: Jingzhou additionally set one colony overseer.

units.zh: 郡皆置太守，河南郡京師所在，則曰尹。
units.en: Commanderies used 'warden' except Henan 'intendant.'
units.literal: Commanderies all set grand wardens; Henan commandery where the capital sat was called intendant.

units.zh: 諸王國以內史掌太守之任，又置主簿、主記室、門下賊曹、議生、門下史、記室史、錄事史、書佐、循行、幹、小史、五官掾、功曹史、功曹書佐、循行小史、五官掾等員。
units.en: Princely kingdoms used interior stewards to perform the duties of commandery administrators and also had chief clerks, chief records offices, gate bandit offices, deliberation students, gate and records clerks, registrar clerks, document assistants, patrol officers, functionaries, petty clerks, gatekeeper aides, merit clerks and assistants, and related posts.
units.literal: Various princely kingdoms used interior stewards to perform the duties of commandery administrators; they also appointed chief clerks, chief records offices, gate bandit offices, deliberation students, gate clerks, records clerks, registrar clerks, document assistants, patrol officers, functionaries, petty clerks, gatekeeper aides, merit clerks, merit clerk assistants, patrol petty clerks, gatekeeper aides, and other posts.

units.zh: 郡國戶不滿五千者，置職吏五十人，散吏十三人；
units.en: Under five thousand households: fifty duty and thirteen extra clerks;
units.literal: Commanderies and kingdoms below five thousand households placed fifty duty clerks and thirteen supernumerary clerks;

units.zh: 五千戶以上，則職吏六十三人，散吏二十一人；
units.en: above five thousand: sixty-three duty and twenty-one supernumerary;
units.literal: above five thousand households then sixty-three duty clerks and twenty-one supernumerary clerks;

units.zh: 萬戶以上，職吏六十九人，散吏三十九人。
units.en: above ten thousand: sixty-nine duty and thirty-nine supernumerary.
units.literal: above ten thousand households—sixty-nine duty clerks and thirty-nine supernumerary clerks.

units.zh: 郡國皆置文學掾一人。
units.en: Every commandery kept a literary aide.
units.literal: Commanderies and kingdoms all placed one literary clerk.

units.zh: 縣大者置令，小者置長。
units.en: Big districts got magistrates; small ones got chiefs.
units.literal: Large counties placed magistrates; small counties placed chiefs.

units.zh: 有主簿、錄事史、主記室史、門下書佐、幹、遊徼、議生、循行功曹史、小史、廷掾、功曹史、小史書佐幹、戶曹掾史幹、法曹門幹、金倉賊曹掾史、兵曹史、吏曹史、獄小史、獄門亭長、都亭長、賊捕掾等員。
units.en: County offices stacked chief clerks through precinct bailiffs—full fiscal and legal desks.
units.literal: There were chief clerks, recorder clerks, chief secretary clerks, gate document clerks, clerks, patrol inspectors, deliberation students, patrol merit clerks, petty clerks, court clerks, merit clerks, petty clerk document clerks, household bureau clerks and clerks, law bureau gate clerks, metals-granary-thieves bureau clerks, military bureau clerks, personnel bureau clerks, prison petty clerks, prison gate precinct chiefs, capital precinct chiefs, thieves-capture clerks, and other seats.

units.zh: 戶不滿三百以下，職吏十八人，散吏四人；
units.en: Under three hundred households: eighteen duty and four extra clerks;
units.literal: Households below three hundred—eighteen duty clerks, four supernumerary clerks;

units.zh: 三百以上，職吏二十八人，散吏六人；
units.en: above three hundred: twenty-eight duty and six extra;
units.literal: above three hundred—twenty-eight duty clerks, six supernumerary clerks;

units.zh: 五百以上，職吏四十人，散吏八人；
units.en: above five hundred: forty duty and eight extra;
units.literal: above five hundred—forty duty clerks, eight supernumerary clerks;

units.zh: 千以上，職吏五十三人，散吏十二人；
units.en: above one thousand: fifty-three duty and twelve extra;
units.literal: above one thousand—fifty-three duty clerks, twelve supernumerary clerks;

units.zh: 千五百以上，職吏六十八人，散吏一十八人；
units.en: above fifteen hundred: sixty-eight duty and eighteen extra;
units.literal: above fifteen hundred—sixty-eight duty clerks, eighteen supernumerary clerks;

units.zh: 三千以上，職吏八十八人，散吏二十六人。
units.en: above three thousand: eighty-eight duty and twenty-six extra.
units.literal: above three thousand—eighty-eight duty clerks, twenty-six supernumerary clerks.

units.zh: 郡國及縣，農月皆隨所領戶多少為差，散吏為勸農。
units.en: Planting season scaled clerks to household counts; extras promoted agriculture.
units.literal: Commanderies, kingdoms, and counties—in farming months all followed registered households in graded differences; supernumerary clerks served as farming encouragers.

units.zh: 又縣五百以上皆置鄉，三千以上置二鄉，五千以上置三鄉，萬以上置四鄉，鄉置嗇夫一人。
units.en: Townships scaled with population—each run by a bailiff.
units.literal: Also counties above five hundred households all placed townships; above three thousand placed two townships; above five thousand placed three townships; above ten thousand placed four townships—each township placed one bailiff.

units.zh: 鄉戶不滿千以下，置治書史一人；
units.en: Small townships added one law clerk;
units.literal: Townships below one thousand households placed one law-editing clerk;

units.zh: 千以上置史、佐各一人，正一人；
units.en: larger townships added clerk, assistant, and rectifier;
units.literal: above one thousand placed clerk and assistant one each, rectifier one;

units.zh: 五千五百以上，置史一人，佐二人。
units.en: above fifty-five hundred: one clerk and two assistants.
units.literal: above fifty-five hundred placed one clerk, two assistants.

units.zh: 縣率百戶置裏吏一人，其土廣人稀，聽隨宜置裏吏，限不得減五十戶。
units.en: Hamlet overseers averaged one per hundred households but flexed in sparse terrain—never below fifty households.
units.literal: Counties normally placed one hamlet clerk per hundred households; where land was broad and people sparse, hamlet clerks were placed as suitable—limited to no fewer than fifty households.

units.zh: 戶千以上，置校官掾一人。
units.en: Thousand-household counties gained an academy clerk.
units.literal: Above one thousand households placed one school clerk.

units.zh: 縣皆置方略吏四人。
units.en: Every county kept four strategy aides.
units.literal: All counties placed four strategy clerks.

units.zh: 洛陽縣置六部尉。
units.en: Luoyang ran six ward captains.
units.literal: Luoyang county placed six division captains.

units.zh: 江左以後，建康亦置六部尉，餘大縣置二人，次縣、小縣各一人。
units.en: Jiankang mirrored Luoyang's six wards; other counties used one or two.
units.literal: East of the Yangzi afterward Jiankang also placed six division captains; other large counties placed two; middling and small counties one each.

units.zh: 鄴、長安置吏如三千戶以上之制。
units.en: Ye and Chang'an staffed at the three-thousand tier.
units.literal: Ye and Chang'an placed clerks according to above-three-thousand-household regulations.

units.zh: 四中郎將，並後漢置，曆魏及晉，並有其職，江左彌重。
units.en: The four palace generals survived Han through Jin and mattered more in the south.
units.literal: Four gentlemen-of-the-palace generals—all Later Han established; through Wei and Jin the posts existed; east of the Yangzi they grew weightier.

units.zh: 護羌、夷、蠻等校尉，案武帝置南蠻校尉于襄陽，西戎校尉于長安，南夷校尉于甯州。
units.en: Wudi posted barbarian commissioners—south at Xiangyang, west at Chang'an, Yi at Ning.
units.literal: Qiang, Yi, Man protectors-general—in tradition Emperor Wu placed Southern Man protector-general at Xiangyang, Western Rong protector-general at Chang'an, Southern Yi protector-general at Ningzhou.

units.zh: 元康中，護羌校尉為涼州刺史，西戎校尉為雍州刺史，南蠻校尉為荊州刺史。
units.en: Yuankang folded commissioners into provincial inspectors—Qiang into Liang, Rong into Yong, Man into Jing.
units.literal: During Yuankang Qiang protector-general became Liangzhou inspector; Western Rong protector-general became Yongzhou inspector; Southern Man protector-general became Jingzhou inspector.

units.zh: 及江左初，省南蠻校尉，尋又置於江陵，改南夷校尉曰鎮蠻校尉。
units.en: South of the river Man posts flickered; Jiangling revived them; Yi commissioner became 'pacify Man.'
units.literal: Early east of the Yangzi Southern Man protector-general was cut; soon restored at Jiangling; Southern Yi protector-general was renamed Pacification Man protector-general.

units.zh: 及安帝時，于襄陽置甯蠻校尉。
units.en: Andi added a pacification commissioner at Xiangyang.
units.literal: When Emperor An ruled, Pacification Man protector-general was placed at Xiangyang.

units.zh: 護匈奴、羌、戎、蠻、夷、越中郎將，案武帝置四中郎將，或領刺史，或持節為之。
units.en: Wudi's four palace generals doubled as governors or credential holders for tribes.
units.literal: Xiongnu, Qiang, Rong, Man, Yi, Yue gentlemen-of-the-palace generals—in tradition Emperor Wu established four gentlemen-of-the-palace generals—some concurrently inspectors, some credential-bearing.

units.zh: 武帝又置平越中郎將，居廣州，主護南越。
units.en: Wudi added a Yue pacification general at Guangzhou for the far south.
units.literal: Emperor Wu also established Pacification Yue gentleman-of-the-palace general, residing at Guangzhou, chiefly protecting Southern Yue.
